criteria.title: Casing — sentence case across all product UI text
criteria.test: **Rule.** Sentence case is the house default for **all** product UI text — buttons/CTAs, menu/tab/nav items, **slide-type and interactive-component names**, headings, tooltips, dialog titles, empty states, messages. Capitalize the **first letter only**; keep proper nouns / brand names / acronyms as-is.

criteria.title: Specific — names the object + what happened
criteria.test: **Rule.** A problem message says *which* thing and *what* about it. Vague, information-free shells are banned as a standalone message: *Something went wrong · An error occurred · Oops / Uh oh · Unexpected error · Some items could not be loaded · bare Failed / Error · Invalid input*.

criteria.title: Actionable — states the next step AND exposes the recovery
criteria.test: **Rule.** Any **recoverable** problem tells the user what to do now and exposes the recovery as a real control when a one-tap recovery exists (Retry / Reload / Log in again / Go back / Contact support). An outcome with no next step is a **dead-end** — the "*so what now?*" reaction.

criteria.title: Human — blameless, jargon-free, no raw codes in the headline
criteria.test: **Rule.** Don't blame the user; keep raw error codes / stack / HTTP status out of the headline (a code belongs in secondary detail); use plain language; lead with the user's goal.

criteria.title: Proportional — severity of wording matches real impact
criteria.test: **Rule.** The words (and the type handed to the surface) match actual impact. A transient, retryable hiccup is a calm info/warning, not a blaring red "Error".

criteria.title: Empty ≠ error
criteria.test: **Rule.** An empty state ("nothing here yet") is a success with no data — encouraging, with a **primary create action**, never an apology or a red alarm. A load **failure** is never disguised as emptiness ("No presentations" when the fetch actually errored hides the Retry the user needs).

criteria.title: Right home & shape
criteria.test: **Scope.** If the surface has **no** recovery-required message and **no** title+body message at all (e.g. a labels-only surface), C7 is **`N/A`** in full — not PASS.

criteria.title: Punctuation: no em dash or en dash
criteria.test: **Rule.** Product copy never uses an em dash (—) or en dash (–) as punctuation. Use a full stop, a comma, a colon, parentheses, or split into two sentences instead.

criteria.title: Real brand identity: the header brand is the product lockup
criteria.test: The top-left brand of any site, microsite or app header (product app, docs site, careers or marketing-style page, internal tool, nav rail) is <aha-product-lockup> with the product name, or with no product attribute when no name is approved; never the logo file or The Splash hand-set next to a text span, never a divider between The Splash and the words. Every other logo (The Splash, the AhaSlides logo, any third-party brand) is taken from the Logo library (design.ahaslides.io/foundations/logo.html, files at /logo/<file>), never redrawn, hand-inlined, recoloured, or replaced by a coloured letter tile or initials square. FAIL if either half is broken.

criteria.title: No dead placeholder shipped as a final state
criteria.test: Every region renders a real asset or a proper empty state — never a permanent 'Loading…' label, spinner, or grey box (e.g. a QR block shows a real code or an explicit 'code unavailable', not 'Loading QR…').

criteria.title: Deliberate hierarchy, one primary action per region
criteria.test: Each region has one clear primary action and a scannable type hierarchy from the scale; not uniform grey-on-white cards of equal weight with evenly-spaced everything.

criteria.title: Shell chrome is tokenised and reuses DS components
criteria.test: Nav rail, top bar, and content region take spacing/radius/colour from --aha-* tokens and fill their slots with DS components (aha-button, aha-icon, aha-avatar, aha-badge, DataTable), never hand-rolled buttons/icons/hex/px.

criteria.title: Active/selected nav state animates on a persistent node
criteria.test: The active nav item and any selected state toggle an attribute/class on a persistent node via motion tokens (--aha-motion-* / --aha-ease-*), never a bare duration literal and never by rebuilding the subtree.

targets.use: every shared component's live DS contract (spec, variants, sizes, states, conformance) — the target look, replacing the frozen Storybook contract.json snapshot
the colour roles and structural values the contracts bind to

criteria.title: Structural values match the measured standard
criteria.test: Radius, height, padding, gap and font family / size / weight for the component under review equal the values in its live DS contract (the <slug>.agent.json feed) — structural values are the same in every binding; any off-by value fails (e.g. radius 6px where the contract says 8px).

criteria.title: Every variant & size is covered
criteria.test: Every variant and size the live DS contract declares is implemented — none of the matrix is missing.

criteria.title: Every sub-part is styled
criteria.test: Every sub-part is styled, not just the outer box: Modal = content + header + body + action footer + close button; Dropdown = menu + item; Input = box + placeholder.

criteria.title: Every interaction state exists
criteria.test: Anything clickable has every interaction state — rest / hover / focus / active / disabled; an absent state fails.

criteria.title: Each state is rendered on the SAME property the standard uses
criteria.test: Each state is rendered on the same property the contract uses (tag active = an outline; radio checked = the tick; checkbox/toggle on = a fill; upload error = the text colour; tooltip = its theme); reproducing a state on the wrong property fails.

criteria.title: Colour is bound as a role for the right context
criteria.test: Structural values are fixed and only colours change per binding: the component uses the colour role for its context — brand (app chrome) or user/neutral (a theme-following canvas) — while danger, positive and brand-pink stay fixed in every binding, all bound to DS colour tokens.

criteria.title: Icon size / box / spacing matches
criteria.test: The icon inside a component has the size, box and spacing the contract fixes and takes the surrounding text colour; the glyph itself is the repo's own asset (exempt).

criteria.title: Verified against the reference picture, not eyeballed
criteria.test: A "matches" claim is evidenced by a screenshot of the built component compared with the DS doc-site render of that component (or the value read from its live DS contract) — not prose, not "looks right"; overlay/interactive parts are captured in their open state.

targets.use: the <aha-icon> API: on-grid sizes, currentColor/token colour, -filled state assets, accessible name
the catalogue of glyph names a view must reuse

criteria.title: One shared icon set — never mixed
criteria.test: Every glyph comes from the single shared icon component (<aha-icon name> in the DS, the shared SVG Icon in an app) and one view uses the system-* outline family consistently — never mixed with @ant-design/icons, Lucide, Heroicons, FontAwesome, Material, Phosphor in a migrated repo, a hand-rolled inline <svg>, or a legacy fill/multicolour glyph.

criteria.title: On-grid size with its paired line-width token
criteria.test: Size is one of the four on-grid values — 12 / 16 / 24 / 32 — via the icon's size prop, so the runtime draws its paired line width (12px 1px, 16px 1.5px, 24px 2px, 32px 2.5px) whatever the glyph's viewBox; never an off-grid size (no 20px) and never a hardcoded one-off stroke width. A glyph may be drawn by hand only when the library has no suitable icon, and then its stroke follows the size: 12px 1px, 16px 1.5px, 24px 2px, 32px 2.5px.

criteria.title: Emphasis via variant; colour via token, not a hardcoded hex
criteria.test: State and emphasis use the -filled glyph variant (or a colour token), never a thickened stroke; colour inherits currentColor or a semantic/brand token (--aha-icon-*, --aha-color-*), never a hardcoded hex on the icon.

criteria.title: Accessibility — labelled, tooltipped, or hidden
criteria.test: An icon-only button carries an accessible name (aria-label or an sr-only label) plus a tooltip when the glyph's meaning isn't obvious; a decorative icon that repeats adjacent text is aria-hidden; state is never conveyed by colour alone.

criteria.title: Standard catalog glyph reused, not a new inline drawing
criteria.test: Common meanings reuse the established catalogue glyph from the live icon registry (validation → warning-circle, success → check-circle, search → magnifying-glass, settings → gear, more → dots-three-vertical, add → plus) rather than a new synonym or a fresh inline drawing; a genuinely missing glyph is added to the DS library; a new drawing is allowed only when the library has no suitable icon.

criteria.title: presenter-app render mode matches the intended fill/outline state
criteria.test: In presenter-app the render mode matches the intended look: an outline-intended system-* glyph uses maintain-color (the default fill: currentColor would blob it), a filled/active glyph or *-fill / *-solid asset stays filled, colour flows through the surrounding element (there is no color prop), and a baked-in stroke hex is fixed at the asset, not with a prop.

criteria.title: A glyph matches the word it stands for
criteria.test: An icon beside a label must depict that label. Mood / sentiment labels use the face set — `system-smiley` (happy / glad), `system-sad-face` (sad), `system-angry-face` (mad / angry). FAIL when a stand-in with a different meaning is used because the right glyph seemed missing (e.g. `system-thumbs-down` for "Sad", `system-fire` for "Mad"). If the registry truly lacks the glyph, add it to the DS rather than borrowing one.

targets.use: the live type scale — font (product), weight (400/600), size, lineHeight and letterSpacing — replacing the frozen typography.json snapshot

criteria.title: Font family matches the role
criteria.test: Product UI text uses the DS product face (Plus Jakarta Sans, the font.product token) for every role; any other family (Poppins, Roboto, Helvetica, SF, Inter) fails — the live DS scale has no Inter label set.

criteria.title: Weight is 400 or 600
criteria.test: Font weight is 400 (regular) or 600 (semibold) only, per the live weight tokens — Display included; 500 / 700 / 800 on a role-based heading or body fails. Text baked into a shared component follows that component's DS contract instead.

criteria.title: Size snaps to the scale
criteria.test: Font size snaps to the DS size tokens (12 · 14 · 16 · 18 · 20 · 24 · 32 · 40 · 48 · 56 · 64); an in-between value (15, 17, 22, 28, 36…) or a rem/em that computes off-scale fails.

criteria.title: Line-height is a unitless ratio matching the role
criteria.test: Line height is a unitless ratio from the DS lineHeight tokens matching the role — 1.2 (H1/H2), 1.3 (H3–H6, blockquote), 1.5 (body, lead) or normal; a px line height, or a ratio that doesn't match the role, fails.

criteria.title: Letter-spacing matches the role's category
criteria.test: Letter spacing matches the role's category per the DS letterSpacing tokens — headlines 0 · subheadings 0.2px · paragraph 0.2px · subtext 0.3px; negative tracking on a heading fails.

criteria.title: Role fits the text's job
criteria.test: The role is chosen by the text's job, not its rough size — page title → heading1 (via <aha-breadcrumb size="page-title">); section → heading2/3; card/dialog title → heading4/5; base UI → body; caption/helper → bodySM — and the five values together match a single DS role.

criteria.title: In scope — every AhaSlides screen and website page
criteria.test: The scale governs every AhaSlides screen and website page: the product apps (presenter, audience, editor, dashboard), docs and internal tools, and every web page (landing, pricing, blog, careers). A web page is never treated as a separate brand surface with its own type; a hero headline takes a display role. Only email, social graphics, video and print creative sit outside the scale.

targets.use: the DS V3 DataTable — header, body, sort, filter, freeze, pagination, cell padding
the colour and radius tokens the grid binds to

criteria.title: It is the shared DataTable — not hand-rolled, not a restyled raw Table
criteria.test: The grid renders through the shared DataTable (AntD <Table> underneath); a raw <table>/<div> grid or a bare AntD <Table> with its own styling fails.

criteria.title: The look is theme-driven — no per-table styling
criteria.test: The look comes from the theme (components.Table), not the call site — a per-table bordered, size, rowClassName zebra, inline header/cell style or ad-hoc container styling fails. A report (the report-image environment: a static report image, or a read-only report page a report routine publishes) is judged on the report-images surface (C11) instead, where white and light grey zebra rows are required (colour rule 3.11).

criteria.title: Header is white with secondary-grey labels
criteria.test: The header is white (Table.headerBg) with secondary-grey labels (Table.headerColor) and a bottom divider — never AntD's default grey #fafafa fill, a tinted header, or default-colour labels.

criteria.title: Body has horizontal dividers only — no zebra, no vertical grid lines
criteria.test: Rows are separated by horizontal dividers only (the border token) — no zebra striping, no vertical cell borders (bordered). A report (the report-image environment: a static report image, or a read-only report page a report routine publishes) is judged on the report-images surface (C11) instead, where white and light grey zebra rows are required (colour rule 3.11).

criteria.title: Behaviour matches DS V3 — sort arrow, filter popovers, freeze, pagination
criteria.test: Where present, behaviour matches DS V3: sort = a single directional arrow (not the dual caret); filter = the checklist (search + Reset/Apply) or Min/Max range popover; freeze = right-click, one column at a time, pinned leftmost with a shadow; pagination = brand-outlined active page + the "N / page" size changer.

criteria.title: Every icon is @phosphor-icons/react — never emoji
criteria.test: Every glyph (help, filter funnel, sort arrow, export, pin, drag handle) comes from @phosphor-icons/react as the DS table contract specifies; an emoji or a glyph from @ant-design/icons or another set fails.

criteria.title: Colour & radius come from tokens — no raw hex/px
criteria.test: Colour and radius in columns, cell renderers, rowClassName and the container bind to theme.useToken() / --aha-* and the radius scale — never a raw #hex, rgb() or magic px radius.

criteria.title: Cell padding is a live 16px — not collapsed to 0 by an undefined token
criteria.test: components.Table.cellPaddingBlock/Inline resolves to 16 (the literal 16 or token.size), not token.padding / paddingSM / paddingM, which are undefined in the AhaSlides token object and collapse the padding to 0.

targets.use: the DS Empty state
the DS Progress (role=progressbar + aria-value*)
the DS loading Skeleton
the DS Result page
the DS FieldError / FieldErrorDisplay
the DS LiveRegion
the DS a11y Progressbar wrapper
useIsMobile() / the DS viewport switch
the DS ErrorPage

criteria.title: Reaches for the canonical DS primitive, not a hand-rolled one
criteria.test: Every registry need is met by its DS primitive — field error → <aha-field-error>; announcement → <aha-live-region>; announced progress → <aha-progressbar>; mobile shape switch → useIsMobile() / <aha-viewport-switch>; full-page error → <aha-error-page>; empty state → <aha-empty>; loading → layout-mirroring <aha-skeleton>. A fresh reimplementation — even a correct one — FAILS.

criteria.title: Correct field-error variant, wired to its input
criteria.test: Forms use the default <aha-field-error> (a11y FieldError); respondent element renderers use variant="respondent" (FieldErrorDisplay: role=alert, aria-live=assertive). Either way the input sets aria-invalid and its aria-describedby points at the error's id (a DS <aha-input> forwards both). FAIL on the wrong variant or missing wiring.

criteria.title: Shape switches use useIsMobile(); styling uses @media (max-width: 767.98px)
criteria.test: A render that changes shape below 768px is gated on useIsMobile() / <aha-viewport-switch>; pure styling uses @media (max-width: 767.98px) directly. FAIL on an ad-hoc breakpoint, the hook driving pure styling, or a 768px / 767px media query.

criteria.title: Accessibility house rules honoured
criteria.test: The live region stays mounted when empty, is assertive + atomic and has no role=alert; an announced progress bar carries role=progressbar + aria-valuenow/min/max + aria-label; skeleton containers carry role=status + aria-busy; visible text uses DS / Typography text, not raw span/p; no state is conveyed by colour alone.

targets.use: the product background pattern: which surface may be non-white, and the token each one binds to
the colour and background rules each criterion cites by id (sections 3, 5 and 7), with what is still open
the --aha-bg-* surface tokens every non-white background binds to

criteria.title: The page and every neutral container is white
criteria.test: The page background and every neutral container (card body, panel, modal and drawer body, table and list row, tab panel) is white or unset (--aha-bg-container), unless it is one of the non-white surfaces judged in C2 to C4: light grey inside or beside the page, Vivid Pink at 5% as a state fill or the one highlighted panel, or black for presenting and viewers. Any other colour on a surface we draw fails here: a brand, pastel or purple fill, a panel painted Vivid Pink, a tint added for emphasis. Misplaced grey, pale pink or black is judged under C2, C3 or C4 and is not flagged again here. In a report (a static report image, or a read-only report page a report routine publishes; environment report-image), number plates in Vivid Pink at 5% and white and light grey zebra table rows pass under rule 3.11; pale pink table rows fail. Presenter and customer content (a slide, an uploaded image, a presenter's own theme) and photos are exempt; an official AhaSlides theme is not.

criteria.title: Light grey sits only inside or beside the white page
criteria.test: Light grey (--aha-bg-layout, --aha-bg-container-secondary, --aha-bg-hover, --aha-bg-container-disabled) is used only on a surface that sits inside or beside the white page: a card, a sidebar, an input field, a table header, the zebra rows of a report table (rule 3.11), the editor workspace around the slide, or a hovered or disabled control. Grey as the background of a whole page, of the layout body behind the content, or of a full-width section fails.

criteria.title: Vivid Pink at 5% is a state fill, plus at most one highlighted panel per screen
criteria.test: Vivid Pink at 5% (--aha-bg-accent) fills a hover or selected state, and at most one highlighted panel on a screen. A second pale pink panel on the same screen, or pale pink as the background of a page or of a full-width section on a screen of the product app, fails. A web page built from full-width sections, wherever it lives (a help article, a sign-up or upgrade page), may use pale pink sections under rules 3.2 to 3.5: they never sit next to each other, and a full white section sits between them. The fill a DS component ships with (a tag, a badge, a selected card) comes from its contract and is not counted as a panel. A report (a static report image, or a read-only report page a report routine publishes; environment report-image) is not a screen of the product app: its number plates (<aha-stat-tile look="accent">, any number of them) in Vivid Pink at 5% pass under rule 3.11, where 3.2 and 3.7 do not apply; its table rows are white and light grey, and pale pink table rows fail. A Report screen inside the product app is still judged as a product screen.

criteria.title: Black backgrounds are for full-screen presenting and viewers only, and there is no dark mode
criteria.test: A black or dark background (--aha-bg-dark, --aha-bg-dark-raised) is the background of full-screen presenting or of a video or image viewer, and of nothing else. A dark page, header, sidebar or panel fails, and so does a dark mode: a theme toggle, a dark theme class, or a prefers-color-scheme: dark restyle of our own. A DS component that ships with its own dark fill (a tooltip, the paywall panel) is judged by its contract, not here.

criteria.title: A status surface is not tinted
criteria.test: No surface is filled or tinted red, yellow, amber, green or blue to show danger, warning, success or information. A status surface stays white (--aha-bg-positive, --aha-bg-negative, --aha-bg-warning and --aha-bg-informative all resolve to white) and carries its meaning with an icon, clear wording and an outline or a black fill. The correct and wrong answer tints (--aha-answer-*, colour rules section 11) on an answer row, a response box or a result banner or chip mark an answer, not a status, and pass.

criteria.title: No gradient as a background or fill
criteria.test: No linear-, radial- or conic-gradient is used as a background or fill. The one exception is an AI feature, where the gradient sits on the border (border-box) and the padding-box fill stays white. The animated Skeleton shimmer between only --aha-bg-hover, --aha-bg-container-secondary and --aha-split is not a gradient fill.

criteria.title: A non-white background comes from a token, never a raw colour
criteria.test: A background that is allowed to be non-white takes its value from a DS token (--aha-bg-*), never a hardcoded #hex, rgb() or hsl() literal, even when the literal is the right colour. A background that is not allowed at all already fails C1 to C5 and is not flagged again here.

criteria.title: A Splash background appears only where it is allowed, and is a DS layout built for its frame
criteria.test: Applies to every surface that carries a splash, in any medium (a product screen, a web page, a video, an ad, a report image). A Splash background (the logo's hooks, enlarged and cropped by the frame) appears only on an empty state or a hero area, never on a dense app screen such as the editor, a table or a settings panel. The file is one from the Background library, one built by build-splash.mjs for the exact frame, or drawn with the Splash in CSS block (brand/colour-rules.json, `splash.cssRecipe`) on the frame it sits in. It is never hand-placed: one of the three DS layouts (centre, right, minimal) sized and positioned by the colour-rules geometry for its own frame, the full 802 by 788 icon, `--splash-across` .5 (centre) or .75 (right). A splash icon given a hand-set `height`, `width`, `right`, `left` or `top` offset, a size and position chosen by eye, or hooks drawn, placed, stretched, cropped or recoloured by hand fail.

targets.use: the colour rules each criterion cites by id: palette, logo, text, buttons, status, charts, what is exempt and what is still open
the --aha-* colour tokens: the only colours a product screen may bind to

criteria.title: Only palette colours appear on anything we draw
criteria.test: Every colour on UI we draw is Vivid Pink, Darker Pink, white, Vivid Pink at 5%, Vivid Pink at 30%, black or a grey, taken from an --aha-* token. Any other hue fails: purple, teal, blue, orange, a retired colour such as Radical Pink, or a near match of a palette colour. Presenter and customer content (a slide, an uploaded image, a presenter's own theme) and photos are exempt; an official AhaSlides theme is not. The purple inside the logo file is the logo, not a UI colour. The correct green and wrong red (--aha-answer-* tokens) pass only where they mark a correct or wrong answer (colour rules section 11) and fail anywhere else. Which palette colour goes where is judged in C2 to C8, not here.

criteria.title: Each palette colour keeps its role
criteria.test: Vivid Pink is the one primary colour. Darker Pink is hover and press only. Vivid Pink at 30% appears in charts only. The 10, 20, 45, 60 and 80% tints appear in illustrations only, never in the interface. Purple appears in the logo only: never in text, buttons, links, states, charts or backgrounds of the product app. A colour used outside its role fails.

criteria.title: Text colour follows the background it sits on
criteria.test: Pink text and pink links sit on white only. On Vivid Pink at 5% or on grey, text and links are the default ink, except an inline link in an Alert or info box message, which is the DS text-link in Vivid Pink (underline on hover and focus). That is the one recorded exception (rule 6.7). On Vivid Pink, text is solid white, never white at a reduced opacity. Pink text on pale pink or on grey fails, and so does see-through white on Vivid Pink.

criteria.title: The primary button is Vivid Pink, and a destructive action is never the primary button
criteria.test: The primary button is Vivid Pink with a white label and turns Darker Pink on hover, with no underline; on solid Vivid Pink the button is the standard secondary Button (on Vivid Pink at 5% it stays the primary). In a group with a destructive action (Delete, Remove) the safe choice (Cancel, Undo) is the primary button. A primary button in any other colour fails, and so does a red or otherwise coloured danger button.

criteria.title: Status carries no hue
criteria.test: No red, yellow, amber, green or blue shows danger, warning, success or information, whether as text, an icon, a border or a dot. Status is shown with an icon, clear wording and an outline or a black fill. A rise is plain black with an up arrow; a fall is white on a black pill with a down arrow; never green and red. The one exception is a quiz answer: the correct green and wrong red (--aha-answer-*) mark a correct or wrong answer with a tick or cross disc (colour rules section 11) and pass; the same colours on a status, a toast, validation or a trend fail. A tinted status background is judged on the background surface (C5 there), not here.

criteria.title: Charts use the four colours, in order
criteria.test: A chart on an app screen uses four colours in this order and never more: Vivid Pink, black, Vivid Pink at 30%, light grey (the brand palette of <aha-chart>). Beyond four series the four repeat with a dashed line or a pattern and a label beside each mark. Anything drawn in Vivid Pink at 30% or light grey shows its value in writing. A fifth colour, a reordered palette or a hand-picked series colour fails. A presenter's own deck palette on the canvas is exempt.

criteria.title: Logos are one colour at rest; file-type icons are one colour
criteria.test: A third-party brand logo in any interface (presenter app, website header or menu, dialog, import source, connect button) is one colour at rest, greyscale (white on a Vivid Pink background), and shows its own brand colours only on hover and keyboard focus, from the Logo library's original-colour file, with the tool's name beside it. Brand colours at rest fail, except on a page that lists other products (Marketplace, an integrations directory), where each logo keeps its own colours in the DS white tile with a grey border, 32px at most, name beside it, and a tool not available yet is greyscale with a Coming soon tag (`<aha-tag color="primary" bordered>`). Brand colour on anything beyond the logo (a button, tag, background or text) fails everywhere. Customer logos in a Trusted by strip are one colour, greyscale or Vivid Pink, one treatment per row. A file-type icon is one colour. The AhaSlides logo is the colour logo on white or the white logo on Vivid Pink, never an all-pink logo on white.

criteria.title: Borders and shadows stay in the palette
criteria.test: Every border, divider, outline, shadow and glow is black, white or a palette colour at any transparency. A shadow or border in another hue (a blue focus glow, a purple card shadow) fails.

criteria.title: In the product app, Vivid Pink at rest fills only each region's primary button
criteria.test: Applies to product app screens only, not the website, the canvas or the audience screens. At rest, Vivid Pink is the fill of the primary button of each region (a page, panel, dialog or drawer) and nothing else: text, borders and icons are the default ink, and pink appears on hover, focus or selection. FAIL if a pink icon, pink border, pink heading or label, or a pink fill other than a primary button shows at rest. Rules that name their own pink pass: inline text links on white (6.6) or in an Alert or info box (6.7), tags (4.6), charts (section 8), the logo and illustrations, the focus ring, the chat launcher, the selected or on state of a control, the one Vivid Pink at 5% highlighted panel (3.7), and fills and marks a DS component ships at rest from its own contract, such as the Paywall upgrade mark, the Stat tile bar, group Avatar grounds, filled Rate stars, Badge primary count, ribbon and active dot, progress and loader fills, the current and finished Steps icons, the Upgrade (positive) and primary-alt buttons, and the highlighted name in a Screen heading greeting.

targets.use: the shared <aha-paywall>: popover anatomy, props, copy, analytics events and upgrade handler (C1–C7)

criteria.title: The gated affordance uses the shared Paywall component
criteria.test: **Rule.** Every pro-gated affordance wraps in `<Paywall>` (or uses `<PaywallCrownBadge>` as the anchor when the feature has no natural anchor). No hand-rolled upgrade modal, tooltip, or popover for monetisation — a bespoke upsell drifts from the presenter app's `UpgradePopover` and breaks the single-source-of-truth contract (PAYWALL-01).

criteria.title: Popover anatomy is exactly correct
criteria.test: **Rule.** The popover is, top to bottom: **crown badge** (the Vivid Pink circle custom `CrownBadge`, 16×16 SVG — *not* the generic Phosphor Crown) + **feature label**; then a **one-sentence value prop**; then the line **"Unlock with the _\<Plan\> plan_."** (plan name bold); then a **single** full-width (`block`) primary **Upgrade** CTA. No secondary "View plans" button, no dismiss link, no multi-paragraph body (PAYWALL-02, -03, -04).

criteria.title: Props contract is honoured
criteria.test: **Rule.** `featureKey` is a stable `snake_case` token (e.g. `custom_survey_url`) reused across analytics and DOM hooks; `featureLabel` and `body` are present; `requiredPlan` is **one of `essential` | `pro`** (defaults to `pro`) — a real tier, not an invented plan name or a display string like "Pro plan" (PAYWALL-05, -07).

criteria.title: Copy rules are followed
criteria.test: **Rule.** **Feature label** is a short noun phrase (the locked feature's name), not a sentence. **Body** is exactly one sentence describing the *benefit* of unlocking (not "This is a Pro feature."), ending in a period. **Unlock line** uses the fixed format — "Unlock with the **\<Plan\> plan**." — not reworded. **CTA** is "Upgrade" by default (a verb); `ctaLabel` is overridden only with a clear reason and stays a verb.

criteria.title: The analytics contract is wired
criteria.test: **Rule.** `PAYWALL_SHOWN` fires when the popover opens and `PAYWALL_UPGRADE_CLICKED` fires when the CTA is clicked — each with props `{ feature: featureKey, plan: requiredPlan }`, and the click event fires **before** navigation or `onUpgrade` runs. Never gate a feature without both events; they are the funnel's denominator and conversion (PAYWALL-06).

criteria.title: Upgrade URL / handler behaviour is correct
criteria.test: **Rule.** The default CTA opens `UPGRADE_URL` (`https://ahaslides.com/pricing`) in a new tab with `noopener,noreferrer`, then closes the popover. When `onUpgrade` is provided it runs **instead** (analytics still fires first) and the popover still closes. The anchor is wrapped in a `<span>` so children don't need to forward refs.

criteria.title: Crown-badge-only anchor used where the feature has no anchor
criteria.test: **Rule.** When a feature has no natural clickable anchor (e.g. a bare field label), the visible anchor is `<PaywallCrownBadge>`, which carries `role="img"` and an `aria-label` (default "Upgrade required"). Don't invent a bespoke lock icon or an unlabelled glyph for this job.

targets.use: the status badge rules: one box, four styles (quiet, emphasis, alert, plain), the three markers, the dot only for published / live and closed, due states, when not to use a badge
the DS status badge element: status, look, marker, icon and the two colour custom properties (C1, C2, C5, C6, C7)

criteria.title: The badge is a marker (dot, icon or none) + a localised text label
criteria.test: **Rule.** A status badge is a single inline element with a visible **text label**, optionally led by one decorative marker: a 16px **icon** from the DS icon registry, a 6px **dot**, or **no marker**. The text is the source of truth. A badge with no text label fails (a bare dot or a bare icon), and so does a badge that shows a dot and an icon together.

criteria.title: Markup is the DS status badge, not an ad-hoc class family
criteria.test: **Rule.** New work renders `<aha-status-badge>` with a `status` from the built-in enum or a `look` (`quiet`, `emphasis`, `alert`, `plain`; `default` is a deprecated alias of `quiet`), and leaves the box alone: no size, padding, radius or font override on the element or its part. Existing markup on the `aha-status-pill` / `aha-status-pill--{status}` / `aha-status-pill__dot` class convention still passes. A bespoke class family (`badge badge-green`), a restyled `<aha-tag>` or a hand-built span fails.

criteria.title: The role=status + aria-label accessibility contract is present
criteria.test: **Rule.** The element carries `role="status"` **and** an `aria-label` equal to the visible label, so the state is announced to assistive tech and **not conveyed by colour alone**. The text label is always present — the dot colour is never the sole carrier of meaning.

criteria.title: The label is sourced from i18n, never hardcoded
criteria.test: **Rule.** The visible label is always a translation lookup — ``t(`survey_status.${status}`)`` or the equivalent namespace for the object — never a hardcoded visible string. Adding a state means adding a translation key (and a `--{status}` modifier), not typing the word.

criteria.title: Colour comes from the status or look, no inline hex
criteria.test: **Rule.** The `status` or `look` attribute (or, in existing markup, the `--{status}` modifier class) drives the badge and marker colour, and it resolves to **semantic tokens**. A status never gets a hue: no green, red, amber or blue badge, no pink anywhere but the alert icon, and no hardcoded hex on the label. The one exception is `--aha-status-badge-bg` with `--aha-status-badge-fg`, set once in a stylesheet for a colour set the app already owns and has had approved (the Report result badges); used to tint a lifecycle, progress or due state, it fails.

criteria.title: The dot only for published / live and closed
criteria.test: **Rule.** The 6px dot marks only the **published / live** and **closed** lifecycle states (and `active` / `inactive`, which follow them): published, live and active on the emphasis style with a dark dot, closed and inactive on the quiet style with a light dot. Every other state takes an icon or no marker (Draft pencil, Scheduled calendar, Archived archive box, the three progress circles). One column may show Draft with its pencil beside Published with its dot. A dot on any other state fails: a dot on Draft, Archived, a progress state, a due state or a counter.

criteria.title: The right style for due states and non-status information
criteria.test: **Rule.** A due state is a badge in this family, set with `look` and `icon`: overdue is **alert**; due today or due soon is **emphasis** with `system-clock`; due in N days is **plain** with no icon; on time is **plain** with `system-check`; N days late is **plain** with `system-clock-late`. Information that is not a status (a counter such as `4/6`, a slide or question type, Unanswered, Time out) uses the **quiet** or **plain** style, with or without an icon and never with a dot. A due state drawn as hand-coloured text or in the wrong style (overdue in quiet, due in N days in alert), a counter or type in emphasis or alert, or a counter with a dot fails.

targets.use: the settings pattern: naming, control choice, grouping by spacing, dependent and gated settings, danger zone, surface choice
the shared settings list, rows and groups (C4, C5, C9)

criteria.title: Setting names are clear noun phrases
criteria.test: Every setting name is a clear noun phrase (or a short when/who/what clause such as "When the module opens") naming what it controls, with no filler leading verb ("Enable", "Allow", "Turn on", "Show", "Toggle") and no trailing-sentence description. Clear beats short: never cut the word that carries the meaning. Group headers are noun phrases or short when/who/what clauses in sentence case with no colon or trailing punctuation.

criteria.title: Correct control — toggle vs checkbox, never mixed
criteria.test: A toggle for an immediate, independent binary; a checkbox for grouped/save-together options or consent (first person). Toggles and checkboxes are **not mixed within one group**. A **segmented (pill) control only for ≈2–4 short one-line options with room to fit**; when the options are **long** (multi-word), **many**, or the control is in a **tight/limited horizontal space** (e.g. sharing a row with an input), a **dropdown/select** — a cramped or overflowing segmented switch breaks the layout. **FAIL** if the control type is wrong for the behaviour, a group mixes toggles and checkboxes, or a **segmented control is used for long/many options or in a cramped space** where a dropdown is required.

criteria.title: Help text is the exception; explanation lives in a `?` tooltip
criteria.test: Always-visible help text appears **only** for a must-see consequence the user can't easily undo — one short sentence (≤90 chars), sentence case, ends with a period, states the consequence not the feature. All other elaboration is a `?` tooltip (≤140 chars, opens on hover **and** keyboard focus **and** tap, no links/buttons/ lists), or omitted. A tooltip is **never** the sole home of a must-see consequence (→ help text) or an error (→ inline copy). **FAIL** on help text used for description/plan-tier/nice-to-know, on an over-long or hover-only `?` tooltip, or on a consequence/error buried in a tooltip. **Panel-level (the most common AI failure):** help text is near-absent across a whole panel — a surface where most or every setting carries a help-text line is the systematic anti-pattern. Count the help lines; more than one is almost always wrong. **FAIL** the panel and convert every descriptive line ("Off means one pick per person", "Display % instead of raw vote counts") into a `?` tooltip. **Redundancy: FAIL** any setting that carries both a `?` help icon **and** a help-text line (same explanation twice — keep the tooltip, drop the line). **Glyph: FAIL** if the help trigger is an info icon (`ⓘ`) instead of a question-mark (`?`) — a help tooltip uses the shared `?` glyph, never an info circle. **Consistency:** every `?` in one panel is the same shared-component glyph at the same size with the same tooltip placement — **FAIL** on mixed help icons, mixed sizes, or inconsistent up/down tooltip direction (AHA-46489, AHA-46544), and on a value's explanation shown as a bespoke hover-state instead of the standard `?` tooltip (AHA-46438). **Styling & arrow: FAIL** a `?` tooltip that isn't the standard/shared tooltip — a custom (non- default) background instead of the dark-navy tooltip token, an **oversized font** (body- or heading-size instead of the small tooltip size), or an **arrow not anchored to the `?` icon** (the pointer floats off to the side instead of landing on the icon).

criteria.title: Grouping & separation come from spacing — no dividers, no cards
criteria.test: Hierarchy and separation use `--aha-size*` spacing tokens (the monotonic 4/16/24/32/48 scale: 4 name→help, 16 sub-setting→parent, 24 between siblings, 32 between groups, 48 danger zone), **not** divider/rule lines and **not** raw px. Plain settings and groups are **never** wrapped in a card or **any container with its own background/tinted fill or border** — a lone toggle/setting row sits directly on the panel surface, not on a grey/tinted rounded pill.

criteria.title: Dependent sub-settings — hidden when parent off, nested when shown
criteria.test: A sub-setting that only applies when its parent is on is **hidden** when the parent is off (not shown disabled — unless the disabled state communicates an upgrade path). When shown, it reads as **nested under** its parent: indented 24px (`sizeLG`) with a 16px gap below the parent (`size`) **and de-emphasized** (label regular 400 in secondary text `--aha-text-secondary` #4A4A4A, where a top-level label is regular 400 in primary text #1A1A1A), and it is never bracketed by its own separators on both sides or wrapped in a container. **FAIL** if a dependent sub-setting is shown disabled instead of hidden, or is rendered at full top-level weight / carded / double-separated.

criteria.title: Plan-gated settings are visible but locked
criteria.test: A setting requiring a plan the user isn't on stays **visible** (not hidden), shown locked: the label, then a crown badge in the place of its normal "?" tooltip (no "?" while locked), and the real control rendered disabled. The badge opens the shared Paywall popover (owned by `aha-design-paywall` — one primary Upgrade CTA, not a bespoke two-CTA one). **FAIL** if a gated setting is hidden, the crown replaces the control, the control stays enabled, the "?" shows beside the crown, or the badge opens a custom popover.

criteria.title: Dangerous settings — last, spacing-separated, danger Button, confirmed
criteria.test: Irreversible/destructive settings sit **last** (bottom of section or a Danger zone at panel bottom), set apart by the largest spacing gap (`sizeXXL`) — **not** a divider. The CTA is an AntD `danger` Button (`colorError`, no hardcoded hex); red is on the button only, never the label/toggle. The action requires a **confirmation modal** before executing (per `aha-design-overlays`) — never a single click/flip, even with an undo toast. **FAIL** on a divider-separated danger zone, a hardcoded-hex or non-danger CTA, red on the label, or a destructive action with no confirmation modal.

criteria.title: Correct surface — panel vs page vs modal vs drawer
criteria.test: Per-object/immediate-effect settings live in the inline editor **panel**; workspace/ account-scope in a **page**; one-time action config in a **modal**; medium-complexity supplements in a **drawer**. **FAIL** if a setting sits in the wrong surface for its scope (e.g. workspace-wide settings crammed into a per-block panel).

criteria.title: Every object renders at its real height
criteria.test: No settings object holds space while rendering nothing visible: an empty section, an empty list wrapper inflating a parent's flex `gap`, or a plugin settings iframe reporting a non-zero height with an empty body / falling back to `height:100%`. An always-rendered wrapper around a conditional list renders only when the list is non-empty; a plugin settings iframe reports its height via `onHeightChange` on mount and every reflow, and reports `0` (or doesn't mount) when there's nothing to show. A gap present on a plugin slide type but not its native equivalent is fixed in the plugin/host iframe layer, **never** by editing a shared editor component. **A third iframe-height mode — the iframe measures the wrong element:** the plugin reports faithfully, but its own mount root (`html`/`body`/`#app`) is CSS-stretched to the viewport (`h-screen` / `100vh` / `height:100%`), so the auto-height reporter reads `#app.offsetHeight` as a full screen and reports a full-viewport height regardless of content — a large empty block below the panel. This **slips past the two checks above** (a height *is* reported, the body *is* non-empty), so when a plugin settings panel shows a large empty block, check the mount root's CSS height *before* the reporting logic (and before chasing per-field margins — a trailing field-gap is usually a minor secondary cause, not the dominant one). The settings-iframe root must shrink-wrap (`height:auto`). **FAIL** on any empty container holding height, a phantom-height iframe (including a mount root forced to viewport height), or a shared-component edit used to chase a plugin-only gap.

criteria.title: Slide-type option list matches the "Items" component
criteria.test: *(Slide-type config only.)* The option list uses the reference row anatomy — drag handle (only when order matters) + text input + optional image button + **on-hover** delete — with a full-width **"+ Add"** button beneath and a `?`-tooltipped noun-phrase section label above. The text input shows a neutral placeholder when empty, a character counter **only on focus**, wraps to multiple lines, and **scrolls internally beyond ~4 lines**. **Reuse-first:** when the panel composes the product's shipped option-row component (in `slide-type-creator`, `@/iframe/settings/OptionRow` / `QuestionList` — verified to encode this anatomy), confirm it IS that component and PASS by construction; a full element-by-element check against the anatomy below (and the build skill's §11 `SETTINGS-*` assertions) is required only when the row is **hand-rolled** — and a hand-rolled row where a shipped component already exists is itself the miss to flag. **The row `<div>` is the single bordered input** — the drag handle is its **first child inside** that one border, the textarea is **borderless**, and the delete **floats just outside the top-right** on hover. These three — **frame, drag handle, delete** — plus the full-width "+ Add" are the **universal core** and must match the reference anatomy on every slide type. A per-option **image** (handled per C11), a **correct-answer checkbox** (scored types: Poll, Quiz), and a **series-colour dot** (types with per-option chart colours) are **legitimate per-type features — do NOT FAIL them** when the slide type actually has that capability. **FAIL** an outer card/box wrapping a separately-bordered text field (box-in-a-box / double border), a drag handle placed **outside/left of** the input, a bordered image-icon box, an always-present in-row delete slot, or **decoration** (a number badge on an unordered set, a decorative label icon). Placeholders match an equivalent existing slide type ("Option 1/2") and are **never** treated as real content (an option still holding its placeholder isn't rendered downstream). Any **numeric/stepper config input** (budget, points, step, limit) enforces a length limit, accepts numbers only, clamps to min/max with an **immediate** fallback (on change/blur, not only on deliberate misuse), and ships pre-filled with the recommended default. **FAIL** on a missing/always-visible delete, a missing "+ Add", a "+ Add" hugged to content width instead of spanning the full panel width, an always-visible or absent char counter on ANY limited text input in the panel (not just option rows — axis labels, titles, notes too: the counter shows only on focus, hidden at rest), an unbounded-growth field, an ad-hoc row shape, a missing/invented placeholder or one rendered as real content (AHA-46484), an unbounded / non-numeric / unclamped / defaultless numeric input (AHA-46440), an **"X of Y" count indicator** next to the section label (e.g. "4 of 8" — redundant; limits are conveyed by the Add/delete disabling, and the reference has no counter), or a **per-option number badge (1, 2, 3…) on an unordered set** where position carries no sequence meaning (reordering is the drag handle's job — numbering falsely implies order; only number when the sequence is genuinely meaningful), or a **fixed unit placed in its own separate framed box** beside a numeric input (a non-changeable unit belongs as an **inline suffix inside the same field** — the shipped `NumberWithUnit`, whose hover stepper, `maxDigits` cap and `errorMessage` line are used rather than re-invented; a bordered box makes a fixed unit look selectable — a changeable unit would be a dropdown per C2, not a static box). **Wrong unit spelling — FAIL:** a **seconds** unit written as `s` (cryptic) or `seconds` (too long) instead of **`sec`** — every unit is its conventional short label, and seconds is always `sec` (§SETTINGS-46).

criteria.title: Image support handled by the right component (per-option vs standalone field)
criteria.test: *(Slide-type config only.)* There are **two** image controls in the library, and the choice depends on whether the image is one cell of an option row or the field itself — using the wrong one (or hand-rolling either) is a FAIL.

criteria.title: Slide-type config follows the reference ordering
criteria.test: *(Slide-type config only.)* The panel is ordered **Question** (title + alignment + optional image + "Add description") → **option list** → **participation constraints** (placed right after the list) → **Time-limit toggle** revealing its duration select (dependent sub-setting) → **collapsed Advanced** section for low-frequency toggles. The standard sections (timing, show/hide results) are **present**, not omitted. Any select/segmented control pre-selects the recommended default and orders its options most-relevant-first (default at the top). Diff against Figma node 9237-9266. **FAIL** if the content/constraints/timing/advanced order is broken, constraints float away from what they constrain, rarely-used settings sit in the default panel instead of Advanced, a standard section is missing (AHA-46508), or a select ships without its recommended default / with the default buried mid-list (AHA-46562).

criteria.title: List wrapper matches the list shape (questions → QuestionList, item-groups → NumberedItem)
criteria.test: *(Slide-type config only.)* A repeatable settings list has **three** library wrappers, and the choice is fixed by the **shape of each item** — using the wrong one, or hand-rolling the accordion / number chip a shipped component already ships, is a FAIL (the list-shape sibling of C11's per-option-vs-standalone image choice): - **A flat set of answer choices for ONE question → `OptionRow`**. - **A list of QUESTIONS, each a prompt plus its own answer choices → `QuestionList`** (the collapsible question editor; it composes `Collapse`, `SettingRow`, `CountedInput`, `OptionRow` and `AddItemButton`, never the reverse). - **A repeatable COMPOSITE item-group the creator counts by ordinal (a Card, a Round) → `NumberedItem`**. Also a FAIL: restyling or replacing the `NumberedItem` number chip — hiding or re-rendering it, or overriding the shadow part with `::part(chip)` (size, colour, ring, shadow) so it mirrors the canvas marker. The chip is the stock 22px muted-grey pill; the settings number is a plain ordinal and never mirrors the canvas marker. Drive it only through the real `n`, `label`, `deletable` and `candelete` attributes.

criteria.title: Settings surface text is localised to the viewer's own app locale
criteria.test: *(Any settings surface that is localised at all — not gated to slide-type config; mark `N/A` only for a surface with no localisation.)* Settings/config text renders in the language of the **person viewing the settings surface**, not an unrelated content language. For a **slide-type plugin iframe** embedded in the AhaSlides presenter app, the right-panel SETTINGS/config text follows the **PRESENTER APP's own UI locale** (`currentUser.presenterLanguage` / the presenter's own locale) — matching the editor chrome the presenter is already using — **not** the deck's **content** language (`presentation.language`), which drives AUDIENCE-facing surfaces (Canvas/Audience copy) only. **FAIL** when a settings panel's own labels/tooltips/help text are driven off content-language state instead of the viewer's own app-locale state — most concretely, a slide-type `Settings.vue` that computes its locale from `presentationProps.value?.language` instead of `currentUserProps.value?.presenterLanguage` (falling back to the deck language only when the presenter locale is unavailable). (AHAM-664 — the presenter's editor was in Vietnamese but the Split the Points settings panel rendered in English because it read `presentation.language`.)

criteria.title: No content-reset / restore-defaults control in a slide-type config panel
criteria.test: *(Slide-type right-panel config only — mark `N/A` for any other settings surface.)* A slide type's right-panel config **must not** carry a "Reset / Restore-defaults / Clear-all" control that re-seeds or wipes the **content the panel itself authors** — the dilemmas, items, buckets, lots or options the presenter typed. This is distinct from C7: C7 legitimises a genuine account/workspace danger-zone action (delete account, wipe workspace data); C15 forbids the **narrower** slide-type case of a button that throws away the panel's own configured content to put the starter defaults back. It fails for three reasons: (a) restoring starter content is **not a setting** — it is a one-shot editor action masquerading as one; (b) it **duplicates** capability the item list already ships — every `OptionRow` / `QuestionList` row carries a per-item delete and direct edit, so "start over" is already reachable without a dedicated control (reuse over rebuild, see CR); and (c) it **collides** with the host's own native "Reset results" control, so two unrelated "Reset" concepts sit in one view. **FAIL** a slide-type Settings panel with a danger `Button` whose handler re-seeds the config from `createDefault…()` / a starter list (labels like *Reset ladder*, *Reset items*, *Restore starter options*, *Reset lots*) — a confirmation modal does **not** rescue it. **PASS** a slide-type panel with no such control; and a legitimate workspace/account **delete-account / wipe-data** danger zone still **PASSES** (judged under C7), because it acts on account-scoped data, not on the content this panel authors.

criteria.title: Group title only over a real group, and no control in a group header
criteria.test: A setting-group / SectionHeader title is semibold and used **only** for a real group of two or more settings — never over a single field or a single list. The header and its action slot carry **no setting control** (no toggle, switch, input, select or button); a control is a settings item (label left, control right). Plain text such as a count may stay in the header. **FAIL** on a title over one field, or any control in the header.

criteria.title: Setting label weight and colour
criteria.test: A setting label (settings item / SettingRow / ModeField label) is regular 400 in primary text (`--aha-text-default` #1A1A1A). A label inside a sub-setting group is regular 400 in secondary text (`--aha-text-secondary` #4A4A4A). Sibling settings sit 24px apart. **FAIL** on a semibold setting label or a nested label in primary text.

criteria.title: Settings controls come from lib/settings.js
criteria.test: Every control in the settings panel is an element that `lib/settings.js` registers (`aha-switch`, `aha-checkbox`, `aha-input`, `aha-counted-input`, `aha-counted-textarea`, `aha-select`, `aha-segmented`, `aha-button`, `aha-option-row`, `aha-setting-row` and the rest of that entry). A raw `<button>`, `<input>`, `<select>`, `<textarea>` or `role="switch"` element, a hand-built toggle, dropdown or option row, or an `<aha-*>` tag that `lib/settings.js` does not load fails. **FAIL** on any of them unless it is a control the DS does not ship, kept with `ds-lint-allow: raw-control (why)` and a reason that holds. The mechanical twin is `node screen-lint.mjs --surface=settings <files>`.

criteria.title: Settings fields — default size, full width when stacked, counter inside on focus
criteria.test: Every field in a settings panel (`aha-input`, `aha-counted-input`, `aha-counted-textarea`, `aha-number-with-unit`, `aha-select`, or their React/Vue forms) is the **default 40px size**, the only size a settings panel uses: `size="large"` or `"lg"` (48px, 16px text, the audience field's size) **fails**, and so does `size="small"` or `"sm"` (32px or 24px); an AntD or slide-type-creator `size="large"` or `"small"` field maps to the DS default when ported. A field in a **stacked** row (label above) **fills the panel width**, also when it sits in a wrapper with helper text; a stacked field left at its 240px intrinsic width, with empty space to its right, fails. A field with a character cap shows its counter **inside the field, only while focused** (`aha-counted-input` / `aha-counted-textarea`); a counter beside or below the field, a counter that is always visible, or `maxlength` on a plain `aha-input` with a hand-made counter fails. **FAIL** on any of them. The mechanical twin for size and `maxlength` is `node screen-lint.mjs --surface=settings <files>` (rules `field-size`, `input-maxlength`); the width and counter placement are judged on the render.

criteria.title: Labels are self-explanatory
criteria.test: Read only the label, group header or option text, with no tooltip, help text or screenshot of the result. **FAIL** if any of them needs that extra context to be understood, is a coined term, a metaphor or a lone abstract noun ("Opening", "Completion", "Behaviour", "Mode", "Display", "General options"), or names a different concept than the same thing elsewhere on the surface or its learner-facing side. **PASS** otherwise. Fix: name the function in the words users already use, with the object and the moment ("When the module opens", "Complete module condition", "Signature").

targets.use: the feedback pattern: toast vs inline vs banner, correct/incorrect states, CSAT
the DS toast (C1)
the DS V3 <aha-alert> inline banner (C4)
the shared CSAT widget (C3)
the shared dismiss ✕ (C6)

criteria.title: Toasts are transient bottom-right pills — auto-dismiss, role=status, portalled
criteria.test: **Rule.** A toast is a **transient, non-actionable confirmation** ("Thanks for your feedback", "Copied"). It is a small `position: fixed` pill at the **viewport bottom-right** that rises from below (never shifting surrounding layout), **auto-dismisses after ~3s** with the timer **cleared on unmount**, carries **`role="status"`** (announced without stealing focus), and — because a `fixed` toast is clipped by any ancestor that establishes a containing block (`transform`, `filter`, `backdrop-filter`, `will-change`) — is **portalled via `createPortal(node, document.body)`** so it stays truly viewport-fixed from every mount point. For ordinary app-level success/info, prefer AntD's `message` / `notification`; the bespoke fixed pill is reserved for custom bottom-right content.

criteria.title: Inline correct/incorrect uses the a11y + semantic-token contract
criteria.test: **Rule.** Result feedback shown in place after an answer carries **`role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`** (informational, not urgent), and colours its container with the **answer tokens** (colour rules 11.1 to 11.3) — border `var(--aha-answer-correct)` / `var(--aha-answer-wrong)` over the 5% tint `var(--aha-answer-correct-tint-5)` / `var(--aha-answer-wrong-tint-5)`, the text staying the default ink (11.2), **never a hardcoded hex**. Right and wrong carry equal weight (11.5); only on a reveal or review screen may a wrong answer add a 2px ring in the wrong red, and the answer key beside a response stays plain. It leads with a strong correct/incorrect label, shows the correct answer and explanation below when incorrect, and exposes stable `data-*` hooks (`data-correct`, `data-element-id`) for testing.

criteria.title: CSAT uses the shared widget, a required source, and best-effort tracking
criteria.test: **Rule.** A satisfaction prompt uses the shared **`Csat`** widget — a binary thumbs rating with an optional follow-up on thumbs-down; **never** a bespoke rating control. It passes a **required `source`** token from the closed **`CsatSource`** union (one per placement) so Mixpanel gets stable, typo-proof segmentation; adding a placement means adding a union member. It emits `CSAT_SHOWN` (once per mount — the response-rate denominator), `CSAT_RATED`, and `CSAT_FEEDBACK_SUBMITTED`, and tracking is **best-effort**: a throwing or uninitialised `track()` must **never** break rendering or block the thank-you toast.

criteria.title: Inline banners use the DS V3 Alert, not a bare AntD Alert
criteria.test: **Rule.** A persistent, in-context message the user may need to act on is a **Design System V3 Alert** — the DS `<aha-alert>` element (`contracts/alert.json`), **not** a bare `<Alert>` with default styling. Each of the five types — `success`, `error`, `info`, `warning`, `branding` — carries its DS `bg-surface` / `icon` token with no border **and a distinct glyph** (colour is never the only signal). Text uses only Plus Jakarta Sans 400 (message/inline link) and 600 (title); the title is **sentence case**. Use an Alert for persistent in-context messages; a toast (C1) for transient auto-dismissing ones.

criteria.title: When NOT to use a toast is respected
criteria.test: **Rule.** A toast that auto-dismisses must **never** be the only place a required message lives. Route by situation: | Situation | Belongs in | |---|---| | Error the user must act on | inline **Alert** banner in context (C4) or an overlay Alert | | Field validation error | `FieldErrorDisplay` / a11y `FieldError` (shared-components) | | Destructive confirmation | a modal (`aha-design-overlays`) | | Full-page failure (not found, expired) | `ErrorPage` (shared-components) |

criteria.title: One shared dismiss ✕ on banners, toasts, notifications and overlays
criteria.test: **Rule.** Every dismiss ✕ on an Alert, Info box, Background task, Toast, Notification, Modal or Drawer is the shared `tertiary icon-only <aha-button> (size xs)` (`contracts/button.json`): a 20 × 20 hit area (radius 6) with the 14px `system-x` glyph in #8A8A8A (`--aha-icon-muted`) that turns #1A1A1A (`--aha-text-default`) on a #F7F7F7 hover fill (`--aha-bg-hover`), top-pinned with its centre 2.5px above the first line's centre so it stays put when the text wraps, and 2px into the container's end padding (Info box: 15px from the right, 11px from the top). A sticky Toast takes it through `dismissibleToast`, a Notification through `dismissibleTitle` with `closable: false`. **FAIL** when any of these surfaces hand-rolls a ✕ (a bare `<button>×</button>`, an inline SVG, a raw icon with its own size or hover, a tertiary or 28 × 28 `<aha-button>` holding a 16px ✕, a circular ✕ — a disc, a 50% or pill radius, or `system-x-circle` used as a control rather than a status icon), shows antd's own message or notification close, or centres the ✕ on the whole card so it drifts down when the text wraps. Modal and Drawer carry it in the title through dismissibleModalTitle / dismissibleDrawerTitle with `closable={false}`. **N/A** when the material has no dismissible feedback surface.

targets.use: the overlay pattern: surface choice, dismiss safety, state reset, async confirm, inline errors
the DS Modal (C1, C3, C5, C7)
the DS Drawer — right placement, responsive width (C4)
the DS Popover (C1)

criteria.title: The right surface is chosen — modal vs drawer vs popover
criteria.test: **Rule.** The surface fits the job: a **modal** for a focused, blocking decision or short flow (confirmations, destructive actions, one-time config); a **drawer** for a detail view or medium-complexity panel that supplements the page (a record's report, distribution settings); a **popover** for a small, anchored, contextual snippet (quick info, a compact input, an upsell) — never for a multi-step flow.

criteria.title: Dismiss behaviour is safety-critical
criteria.test: **Rule.** **Destructive / data-loss overlays MUST NOT dismiss on outside/mask click** — set `mask={{ closable: false }}` so a stray backdrop click can't trigger destruction, leaving `keyboard` (Esc) and the explicit **X** button as the only dismiss paths. Non-destructive overlays may allow mask-close. While an async action is in flight (`busy`), cancel/close is **disabled or suppressed** (`onCancel`/`onClose` suppressed) so the user can't dismiss mid-operation.

criteria.title: State resets between opens
criteria.test: **Rule.** The overlay sets `destroyOnHidden` (Modal) / `destroyOnClose` (Drawer) so transient state — form input, error text, busy flag — resets between opens. If the instance can stay mounted, local error and busy state are also cleared explicitly on open rather than relying on unmount alone.

criteria.title: Side drawers use placement=right and responsive width; list-launched surfaces are a bottom sheet
criteria.test: **Rule.** Side drawers default to `placement="right"` with **responsive width** `width={isMobile ? '100%' : <fixed>}` (e.g. `720`) driven by `useIsMobile()` — full-bleed on mobile, fixed panel on desktop. The width is a **prop**, not gated through CSS. A launch surface opened from a list of objects (one click on a deck) is instead a **bottom sheet**: `<aha-drawer placement="bottom">` in every framework — full width, 48px top gap that closes on click, 16px top corners, grab handle, Esc, ✕ and swipe down close it, full page under 768px. Never a sheet hand-built from a fixed `div`.

criteria.title: Async confirm follows the busy-guard / await / stay-open pattern
criteria.test: **Rule.** When `onConfirm` returns a promise, the overlay: (1) guards re-entry (`if (busy) return`), sets `busy`, clears prior error; (2) `await`s the action; (3) on rejection **stays open** and surfaces the error inline (see C6), then clears `busy`; (4) on success the caller closes the overlay. Never close a destructive overlay before its action resolves, and never fire-and-forget.

criteria.title: Errors surface inline, never a nested modal
criteria.test: **Rule.** Failures are surfaced **inside** the overlay with an inline **DS V3 Alert** (`AhaAlert type="error"` — the banner component owned by [[aha-design-feedback]], **not** a bare AntD `<Alert>` with default styling). This judge owns *placement* (error goes inline, overlay stays open); feedback owns the Alert's *styling*. **Never** stack a second modal on top to report an error, and never downgrade it to a transient toast. The overlay stays open on failure so the user can retry without re-opening.

criteria.title: Destructive confirm uses a danger-styled button
criteria.test: **Rule.** A destructive confirmation uses `okButtonProps={{ danger: true, type: 'primary', loading: busy }}` — the **dark danger styling lives on the action button**, never on the title or body — and Cancel, the safe choice, is the primary button (`cancelButtonProps={{ type: 'primary', disabled: busy }}`), disabled while busy. For confirmations the title is a **question** ("Delete this survey permanently?").

targets.use: the presenter-canvas pattern: framed vs full-canvas, declared actions, deck ink and fonts
the colour and type tokens every hard-coded colour/font check binds to (C1, C2)

criteria.title: No hard-coded colours or fonts
criteria.test: **Rule.** All colour and font values come from xprops, and colour reaches a hand-built element only as the `--aha-deck-*` ladder that `applyCanvasDeck` writes from them: - `xprops.slide.textColour` becomes `--aha-deck-ink` and its tints (`-ink-secondary`, `-line`, `-stroke`, `-fill`, `-surface`, `--aha-deck-container-*`, `--aha-deck-modal-*`) - `xprops.slide.baseColour`, `xprops.slide.backgroundImage` - `xprops.presentation.fontFamily` - `xprops.presentationColorPalette[n]` is the accent (`--aha-color-primary`) and the fill of charts and data, with `presentationLighterColorPalette[n]` for the lighter shade. **FAIL** when a hand-built element mixes its own shade of the ink (`color-mix()` or an opacity on `textColour`), paints with a product colour token (`--aha-text-*`, `--aha-border-*`, `--aha-bg-*`, `--aha-surface-*`), or hard-codes a colour or font. **PASS** when the same element reads the ladder (`--aha-deck-container-fill` for a panel, `--aha-deck-ink-secondary` for secondary text), or is a DS element such as `<aha-canvas-count>` that is already inked. The role to token table is on the Deck tokens page.

criteria.title: Semantic state colours applied to the indicator, NOT the chart
criteria.test: **Two different colour jobs on a canvas — keep them separated:** 1. **Chart / visualization layer** (bar fills, ring segments, area shading, plot dots). These pull from `xprops.presentationColorPalette` so the chart feels native to the deck's brand. They carry magnitude/proportion, NOT meaning. 2. **State indicator layer** (the ✓ / ✗ icon, status badge, border accent, label chip that announces correctness). This carries meaning. It pulls from semantic tokens that the plugin has bundled into its own build. **Rule.** Apply semantic state colours (success-green, error-red, warning, info) to the **indicator** — not to the chart. Painting the bar itself in `colorSuccess` / `colorError` (or hard-coded `#22C55E` / `#EF4444`) is the violation, even when the intent is correct, because: - The bar fights the deck's brand colour identity on any non-green/non-red palette. - The state is conveyed by colour layered onto a visualization, not by a dedicated signal — collapses the "non-colour cue" criterion (C6) into the chart.

criteria.title: Action buttons in the right place: declared for the host bar on a built plugin, in-canvas on the Developer Platform
criteria.test: **Rule.** On a **built** slide plugin, Previous / Next / Summarise / Reset and any other slide-specific actions are **declared** via the plugin manifest's `actions` array and **painted by the host** in the presenter control bar (`PresenterControlBarNew.vue`, region `ncb-center` portal, rendered through `NcbPluginActions.vue`); that canvas iframe never contains the action buttons themselves. A **build-less Developer Platform** slide type (presenter.html / audience.html / settings.html loading `lib/all.js`) has no manifest actions: its presenter controls render **inside** the canvas as DS `<aha-button>` elements (sized by C17) — that placement PASSes here, and a raw `<button>` there FAILs.

criteria.title: Action shape correct, with sensible variant hierarchy
criteria.test: **Rule.** A built slide plugin does NOT pick a button size — the host renders every declared action via the `<aha-antd-button>` design-system wrapper at whatever size the host configures; the plugin's job is to declare the right **data** (label, variant hierarchy with ≤1 primary, boolean disabled/loading). On the Developer Platform the same variant hierarchy applies to the in-canvas `<aha-button>` row.

criteria.title: Legible against the REAL background — WCAG AA contrast, readable size, AND real text
criteria.test: Three failure axes, one goal: the slide is read from a distance, so meaningful text and shapes must **contrast enough**, be **big enough**, AND **read as normal running text** (not a decorative treatment) to be understood from the worst seat. Any one axis failing → C5 FAIL. Contrast is judged against the real composited background, including text over a deck background image; if it falls below the floor, fix it with a `textColour` or photo that clears the floor, not by adding a layer behind the text.

criteria.title: Non-colour cue paired with every colour-bearing signal
criteria.test: **Rule.** If colour carries meaning (right/wrong, winner/loser, warning/normal, correct/incorrect), it MUST be paired with at least one of: - An **icon** (✓, ✗, crown, alert) — **preferred**: compact, language-neutral - A **label** ("Correct", "Incorrect", "Winner") — heavier, brings an i18n surface - A **shape** (border style, pattern, outline) - **Position** (winner = top of list)

criteria.title: Framed vs full-canvas chosen intentionally in the manifest
criteria.test: **Rule.** The plugin's manifest declares `setting.enableFullScreen` explicitly: - **Framed** (`setting.enableFullScreen: false`): host renders the question title / description / question image at the top of the stage; the canvas iframe only renders the answer/interaction area. - **Full-canvas** (`setting.enableFullScreen: true`): host hides its chrome; the canvas iframe renders its own title and full layout, still honouring theme and accessibility.

criteria.title: Plugin initialises its locale from `presentation.language` xprop
criteria.test: **Rule.** Every user-visible string passes through i18n. The plugin runs in its own iframe with **its own i18n instance** — it does NOT inherit the host's locale state. The plugin must explicitly **initialise its locale from `xprops.presentation.language` (or `xprops.currentUser.presenterLanguage`) at startup, and react to changes**.

criteria.title: Visual restraint — no AI-generated design tells
criteria.test: Five specific choices make a canvas read as machine-generated — or plain broken — rather than designed. **Any one → FAIL.**

criteria.title: Keyboard-shortcut affordances
criteria.test: **Scope.** This criterion is about controls the **canvas renders itself** — a bespoke overlay the host control bar (NCB, §C3) doesn't paint: an animated game's play / pause, a reveal toggle, a music-mute button, a settings popover. Host-painted NCB actions get their shortcut chips, focus order, and sound from the host and are out of scope here. **Rule.** a. A modal / overlay / popover moves focus in on open, traps Tab / Shift+Tab, and returns focus to the trigger on close. b. Every actionable button shows its shortcut as a chip: a **24 × 24 square, radius 4**, key 14px / 400; a longer key keeps the 24px height and grows with 6px side padding — never a wide pill. On `<aha-button>` it is the `shortcut` attribute, not a hand-made `<kbd>`. c. A labelled button shows the chip **inline** after its label, never only in a hover `title="Press X"`. d. An icon-only button sits in a tooltip that shows its **name followed by the shortcut chip** (`<aha-tooltip size="lg" text="Mute music" shortcut="M">`), and its `aria-label` is the name plus the shortcut in parentheses, `Mute music (M)`. Any sub-rule missed → FAIL.

criteria.title: Deck-ink fallback reads on the surface it lands on
criteria.test: **Scope.** Ink written as `xprops.slide.textColour ?? <fallback>` (or `textColour || …`). The default deck leaves `slide.textColour` **unset** — the host paints body text itself and forwards nothing — so the fallback is the **real paint path on the most common deck**, not an edge case. This criterion checks the fallback branch specifically; C5's contrast axis measures the `textColour`-**set** path. A canvas that never falls a deck ink back onto a bounded surface PASSes vacuously. **Rule.** **FAIL** when the fallback is a **fixed colour** (`?? '#fff'`, `?? ahaBrand.white`, `?? '#313131'`, `?? colorError`, any constant) **AND** that ink sits on a **bounded filled surface whose fill can be either polarity** — a disabled-grey / state-tinted box, a coloured chip, a card. A fixed fallback clears contrast on one polarity and **vanishes on the other** the moment the deck is a default theme (`textColour` unset): a `?? white` label disappears on a light box, a `?? '#313131'` label on a dark one. **PASS** when the fallback is **derived from that surface's own background** via a luminance flip — `readableInkOn(fill)` / `luminance(bg) > 0.45 ? dark : light` — so it reads whichever way the box is painted. Ink that falls back on the **deck background itself** (not a bounded surface) may keep the flat `#313131` / `#ffffff` deck fallback — this criterion is about ink on a *slide-painted surface*.

criteria.title: Full-canvas slide renders the host title itself
criteria.test: **Scope.** Fires only when the manifest declares `setting.enableFullScreen: true` (full-canvas). A **framed** slide (`enableFullScreen: false`) PASSes vacuously — the host draws the title bar, so the canvas must not. This criterion is the specific, most-missed half of C7: C7 checks the *manifest declaration* is explicit and coherent; **C12 checks the one thing behind it that a reviewer most often skims past — that a full-canvas canvas actually paints the presenter's title.** **Rule.** In full-canvas mode the host hides **all** its chrome, including the title bar it renders in framed mode. So the presenter-entered title / question — forwarded to the plugin as the **title xprop (`slideProps.title`)** — has no host surface to land on. If the canvas doesn't render it itself, the title the presenter typed is collected in the editor and then **silently dropped on the presenting screen**. A full-canvas canvas therefore **MUST read `slideProps.title` and render it** somewhere legible in its own layout. Rendering only per-item prompts, answer labels, or a decorative/static heading while **never reading `slideProps.title`** is a **FAIL**.

criteria.title: On-canvas text clears a legible size floor
criteria.test: **Rule.** Every meaningful on-canvas text — the title / question, answer text, data values, status lines, option labels, button labels, tooltip names — uses a **fixed-px type-scale role at or above the 16px caption floor**, the same scale C5 defines (caption `text-base` 16 · body `text-lg` 18 · subhead `text-2xl` 24 · title `text-5xl` 48 · hero `text-7xl` 72). FAIL on meaningful text below 16px, a `vh`/`vw` font-size, a `clamp()` px floor or `text-xs`/`text-sm`. **The one exception:** the 14px / 400 key inside a shortcut chip (`<aha-button shortcut>`, `<aha-tooltip shortcut>`, or the same chip on a library button) PASSes; its label or tooltip name beside it stays 16px.

criteria.title: Deck font is LOADED into the iframe, not just referenced
criteria.test: **Scope.** Fires whenever the canvas renders text in the deck font — it binds `xprops.presentation.fontFamily` (directly, or via a `deckFont` computed) to an element's `font-family`. A canvas that renders no text, or renders only in the bundled default face, PASSes vacuously. **Rule.** The host forwards only the deck font's **NAME** (`xprops.presentation.fontFamily`), never the font file. A slide plugin is a **cross-origin iframe**, and an iframe does **not** inherit its parent document's `@font-face` rules — so `font-family: <deck name>` alone points at a face the iframe has never loaded, the browser falls back to its default **serif** (Times), and **every** text on the slide renders in it. The canvas MUST therefore also **load the face**: inject the deck font's stylesheet into the iframe. In `slide-type-creator` that is the shared `useDeckFont(fontFamily)` helper — it adds the Google-Fonts `<link>` for the requested family, is idempotent, and no-ops for the bundled Plus Jakarta Sans. Binding `fontFamily` **without** loading the face is a **FAIL**.

criteria.title: Canvas content is padded, not clipped by an under-padded container
criteria.test: **Rule.** Meaningful content — a title, a progress / "rung" badge (`RUNG 1 OF 4`, `Q1 of 5`), a status line, the first row of a list — must sit inside adequate container padding and render **fully visible**. Nothing important is sliced by an under-padded container, an `overflow`-bounded box, or a flex column that squeezes or overflows its top item.

criteria.title: A per-round advance stepper uses the default (secondary) variant, never the primary accent
criteria.test: **Rule.** A slide action the presenter clicks to advance **one step at a time through many rounds** — This or That's *Next pair*, a per-question *Next*, a dilemma ladder's *Next dilemma / rung* — is workhorse NAVIGATION, not a climactic CTA.
