It MUST take the **default / secondary** variant (the solid white-background button), never the filled **primary** accent — and that holds in **both** places the control can appear: - **the declared action** in the plugin manifest — `variant: 'secondary'` (or omit `variant`; secondary is the default), never `variant: 'primary'`; - **the in-canvas FALLBACK button** the slide renders itself when the host action bar is off (playground / flag off) — the Ant `<Button>` must be the DEFAULT button, never `type="primary"` (and never a bespoke filled-accent button). The fallback must MIRROR the declared variant, or the same control shouts an accent in the playground while it is quiet in the product.

criteria.title: An in-canvas presenter control is <aha-button> sized by attribute (size="lg"), never resized through ::part
criteria.test: *(Fires when the canvas renders its own presenter controls — the Developer Platform's in-canvas row or a built plugin's fallback. N/A otherwise.)* Each control is a DS `<aha-button>` whose size comes from the `size` attribute — `size="lg"` (40px, 8px corners, 16px / 600 label; icon-only 40 × 40) — and whose colours come from `applyCanvasDeck` (`lib/canvas.js`): the deck accent on the primary, a black or white label by contrast, hover 12% and pressed 22% darker, no hover shadow. FAIL on `size="xl"` (the retired 52px canvas size) or any other size, on any `::part(button)` rule (or inline style) that sets height, padding, font-size or radius, and on recolouring through `::part` or a per-slide accent variable instead of `applyCanvasDeck` / `--aha-color-primary`. Also FAIL on `variant="tertiary-deck"` sitting directly on the photo of a photographic deck (`slide.backgroundImage` set): the action becomes a `secondary-deck`. PASS for a `tertiary-deck` on a photographic deck when it sits on a bounded surface the slide paints with its own fill (card, panel, popover, sheet, chip), so the photo is not its direct backdrop, and its glyph clears 3:1 (a text label 4.5:1) against that surface as rendered over the photo; a translucent surface counts when it clears that floor, and FAILs when the photo shows through enough to drop below it.

criteria.title: A framed slide over a photo keeps the deck showing — no slide-wide scrim
criteria.test: *(Fires on a framed slide — `enableFullScreen: false` — rendered with `slide.backgroundImage` set. N/A otherwise.)* The root and the whole answer area stay transparent. A scrim, panel or backdrop painted behind the entire board (e.g. an `#app.scrim` class added whenever a background image is set) FAILs. Only bounded surfaces such as cards may be opaque; text over the photo needs no backing.

criteria.title: One accent per deck — palette[0] on --aha-color-primary, same on every surface
criteria.test: The deck accent is `presentationColorPalette[0]` published as `--aha-color-primary` on `:root` (with the `--aha-button-primary-*` hover / press / text tokens), so canvas, audience and every `<aha-button>` show the same colour. FAIL when a surface recomputes the accent (mixes it toward the ink until a contrast target, darkens it in steps, uses a 'towardInk' variant for selection), when two surfaces show different 'primary' colours, or when a semantic colour (success teal, error red) is used as a data / series / column colour. Picking only the LABEL ink by contrast is correct. So are the hover and pressed shades `applyCanvasDeck` (canvas) and `applyDeck` (audience) derive from the accent: the rest fill is still the accent itself.

criteria.title: Borders are hairlines and radius follows the DS scale
criteria.test: A bounded white card has a 1px neutral border (`--aha-border-default` #E3E3E3) and 12px radius (`--aha-radius-lg`); a deck-owned surface (chip, field, track) a 1px `currentColor` 10% hairline, no 20% exception; dashed empty states 1px; option tiles, inputs and buttons 8px. FAIL on 2px (or heavier) outlines on cards, tiles, chips or inputs, on borders at heavy ink (e.g. 14–55% textColour at 2px), or on a rectangular container above 12px radius.

criteria.title: One fixed dark ink: #1A1A1A
criteria.test: Wherever the slide uses a fixed dark ink (labels on a light fill, the dark half of a contrast pick, a fallback ink), it is `--aha-text-default` #1A1A1A. FAIL on the retired indigo `#1A1A2E` used as text ink, or on a second near-black (`#000`, `#111`) used alongside it.

criteria.title: Interactive states animate with motion tokens on persistent nodes
criteria.test: Every hover, selected, expanded or revealed state transitions with `--aha-motion-*` durations and `--aha-ease-*` curves (no bare `.2s` literals), declared on nodes that persist across updates. FAIL when interactive states snap (no transition at all), or when the view is rebuilt with `innerHTML =` / `replaceChildren()` on each state change so the transition can never fire.

criteria.title: Stage steppers and comboboxes are the DS elements, current stage in ink
criteria.test: *(Fires when the canvas shows a stage / round indicator or a type-to-pick field. N/A otherwise.)* A stage indicator is `<aha-stepper>` (size="lg" on the canvas, `color` set to the deck ink) and a type-to-pick field is `<aha-autocomplete>`, both from `lib/all.js`. FAIL on hand-rolled stepper pills (`.step` spans / `<li>`s styled per slide) or a hand-built `<input>` + `<ul>` suggestion list, and FAIL when the current stage is filled or outlined with the primary accent (`--aha-color-primary`, palette[0]) — the accent belongs to the one action that advances the flow; the current stage is marked with ink.

criteria.title: Keyboard-only operation
criteria.test: *(Applies to every canvas with a presenter interaction, in Standard and Immersive UI styles. A display-only canvas with nothing to press, hover or drag passes vacuously.)* Slide Plugin Policy (POLICY.md) section 6: the presenting view supports full no-mouse, no-touch operation. **Rule.** a. Every presenter interaction works with the keyboard alone: each control is reachable by Tab in a sensible (reading) order, shows a visible focus ring, and activates with Enter or Space, a declared shortcut, or a host-painted action. A `<div>`/`<span>` with a click handler and no `tabindex`/role/key handler FAILs. b. Anything shown on hover (a tooltip, a result label, a highlight, a reveal) is also shown on keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`); a hover-only reveal on a non-focusable element FAILs. c. Any drag, draw, swipe or other pointer gesture has a keyboard alternative (arrow keys, Move up / Move down buttons, Space to pick up and drop); a pointer-only gesture FAILs. d. No keyboard trap: Tab always leaves the canvas controls (a modal's contained Tab cycle is the C10 focus-trap and passes when Esc or a Close control exits). e. The canvas never swallows the deck's navigation and clicker keys (ArrowRight / ArrowLeft, PageDown / PageUp, Space): no blanket `keydown` handler that calls `preventDefault`/`stopPropagation` on them, except to claim a build step through the SDK, or while a widget the presenter has explicitly focused owns the key. Any sub-rule missed → FAIL. C10 covers the shortcut chips, tooltips and focus-trap of bespoke controls; this criterion is the reachability test for every interaction, not only those.

targets.use: the audience-screen pattern: mobile-first column, self-rendered states, deck-tracking controls, text economy
the colour and type tokens every hard-coded colour/font check binds to (C1, C2)

criteria.title: No hard-coded colours or fonts
criteria.test: **Rule.** All colour and font values come from xprops, and colour reaches a hand-built element only as the `--aha-deck-*` ladder that `applyDeck` writes from them: - `xprops.slide.textColour` becomes `--aha-deck-ink` and its tints (`-ink-secondary`, `-line`, `-stroke`, `-fill`, `-surface`) - `xprops.presentation.fontFamily` - `xprops.presentationColorPalette[n]`, `xprops.presentationLighterColorPalette[n]` as the accent. **FAIL** when a hand-built element mixes its own shade of the ink (`color-mix()` or an opacity on `textColour`), paints with a product colour token (`--aha-text-*`, `--aha-border-*`, `--aha-bg-*`, `--aha-surface-*`), or hard-codes a colour or font. **PASS** when it reads the ladder.

criteria.title: Semantic state colours bundled, applied to the indicator
criteria.test: **Rule.** Meaning-bearing state colours (correct/incorrect, success/error, submission feedback, validation) must come from the plugin's own **bundled** design-system tokens. They do NOT come from: - The deck's palette (`xprops.presentationColorPalette[n]`) — a palette may not contain a usable red/green, so state would silently shift per deck. - Host CSS variables (`--aha-colorSuccess` etc.) — these don't cross the iframe boundary. - AntD's `theme.useToken()` — React+v5 API, not available in this stack.

criteria.title: Mobile-first single column + height reported via onHeightChange
criteria.test: **Rule.** The audience layout must be: - **Single column.** No side-by-side panels assuming desktop width. - **Fluid up to host's max-width** (host enforces ~710–840px in framed mode); no fixed device-width assumptions. - **No horizontal scroll** at the narrowest phone width (~320px). - **Height reported via `onHeightChange(h)`** whenever content changes size; no fixed-height containers that assume a specific device.

criteria.title: Plugin self-renders submitted / waiting / correct-incorrect; host utilities used where they fit
criteria.test: **Rule.** For built-in slide types the host overlays a "Waiting…" screen after submit. **Plugins do not get that** — the iframe stays mounted and the plugin must render the post-submission UX itself: - **Just submitted** — ✓ confirmation rendered inside the iframe - **Waiting for the next slide** — same surface, calm hold state - **Quiz correct/incorrect** — state colour on indicator (icon), bar in palette - **Pre-submission empty state** — input affordance with placeholder copy, not a giant empty zero

criteria.title: WCAG AA contrast + touch targets + mobile readability
criteria.test: **Rule.** Three thresholds on the audience surface: **Contrast** — every meaningful text and shape meets WCAG AA against the **plugin-chosen background**: - 4.5:1 floor for text (3:1 for large text ≥18pt / 14pt bold) - 3:1 floor for meaningful non-text shapes (bar fills, status dots, dividers)

criteria.title: Non-colour cue paired with every colour-bearing signal
criteria.test: **Rule.** If colour carries meaning (right/wrong, correct/incorrect, submission state, leader/winner), it MUST be paired with at least one non-colour cue. **Prefer icon** as the cue — compact, language-neutral.

criteria.title: Framed vs full-canvas declared explicitly in the manifest
criteria.test: **Rule.** The plugin manifest declares `setting.enableFullScreen` explicitly: - **Framed** (`setting.enableFullScreen: false`) — host renders question image, title, description, audio button, countdown progress *above* the iframe. The audience iframe owns the answer area only. **Plugin must NOT render its own title** in this mode — duplicates the host's. - **Full-canvas** (`setting.enableFullScreen: true`) — host hides chrome. Plugin renders the entire surface, including its own title.

criteria.title: Plugin i18n initialised from xprops.presentation.language
criteria.test: **Rule.** The audience iframe has **its own i18n instance** (separate document, separate bundle). It does NOT inherit the host's locale state. The plugin must explicitly **initialise its locale from `xprops.presentation.language` at startup** (fallback `xprops.currentUser.presenterLanguage`) and update when the host emits a change.

criteria.title: Submit button matches the standard spec
criteria.test: **Rule.** Every built-in audience slide type uses one consistent submit-button look + behaviour (the host design system's `aha-antd-button` in the "primary-alt" variant). That component doesn't cross the iframe boundary, so plugin authors build their own — but the in-iframe button MUST match the shared spec (visual + behaviour + wiring), or audience experience drifts per slide type. On the build-less Developer Platform the design system does cross the boundary (the iframe loads `lib/audience.js`): the submit is `<aha-audience-submit>`, and a raw `<button>` or a hand-ported copy of its CSS FAILs.

criteria.title: Visual restraint — no AI-generated design tells
criteria.test: Three specific choices make the audience UI read as machine-generated. **Any one → FAIL.**

criteria.title: Transform / animation stays inside the reported box
criteria.test: **Rule.** `onHeightChange` reports the plugin's **resting** box, and the host shrink-wraps the iframe to that height, painting nothing outside it. Any transform that lifts content past the reported edges — a swipe tilt, a drag ghost, a hover pop, a settle bounce (`rotate`, `translateY(-n)`, `scale(>1)`) — gets **clipped by the iframe**. The transformed element's bounding box, at its most extreme animation frame, must still fit inside the reported height: headroom is budgeted for it, and the transform is capped small enough to live in that headroom. Prefer a cap that costs zero downward shift (a smaller tilt angle raises the leading corner far less) over a bigger transform that forces a taller box and pushes content down.

criteria.title: Swipe / drag gesture stays smooth (60 fps)
criteria.test: **Rule.** A card the audience drags or flings re-renders every frame while it moves. Two things reliably make that laggy on a real phone, and both are FAILs: 1. **An expensive continuous effect stays on the moving element.** A `backdrop-filter: blur()`, a large `box-shadow`, or any `filter` on the dragged / flung element is re-sampled every frame → dropped frames. It must be **dropped while the element is moving** (a `dragging || flinging || settling` flag nulls it out) and restored when it settles. Only `transform` and `opacity` may animate (compositor-only); no per-frame `width` / `height` / `top` / `left` / `margin`, and `will-change: transform` on the element. 2. **Commit is distance-only.** A fast flick that hasn't crossed the distance threshold springs back — reads as an unresponsive / laggy swipe. The release must commit on **distance past the threshold OR a flick-velocity** (pointer px/ms) in that direction.

criteria.title: Text economy — no redundant text; instructions are unboxed body text
criteria.test:
**Rule.** Every word on the audience surface must add information the controls don't, and instructions stay quiet. Two facets: 1. **No label, header, or connective that merely restates an adjacent control.** If the choices are already on labelled controls ("True" / "False" buttons), a header repeating them ("True or False") and a divider word between them ("OR") are pure redundancy — the buttons are the prompt and a binary choice is self-evidently one-or-the-other. Delete them. 2. **Micro-instructions are the shortest phrase, in the DEFAULT audience body, not in a prominent container.** A hint ("Tap or swipe to answer") is one line of **16px, regular (400) weight, the deck's own text colour** — the default body treatment — never a full-width pill, tinted card, shadowed chip, or button-shaped box. Prominent chrome makes the hint compete with the controls; a semibold, sub-16px, or muted-grey hint is off the default body (AHAM-701 issue 2a — the reporter's "Good" is 16px regular deck text colour). **CONSISTENCY across a slide family is part of the rule:** two slides whose instructions differ in size, weight, or colour FAIL even if each looks fine alone. The reliable way to hold this is ONE shared instruction component (`InstructionLine`) that every slide imports — a hand-styled `

` on one slide and the component on another is exactly the drift that was reported.

criteria.title: Host-owned transient notices not re-rendered in the iframe
criteria.test: **Rule.** The host owns two round-end announcements; the plugin must not duplicate either inside the iframe (framed mode).

criteria.title: Shared components used, not rebuilt
criteria.test: **Rule.** Where the repo ships an audience component library, the surface is built FROM it. A control that duplicates a library component's job FAILs — and it FAILs even when it renders identically today, because the library is where the cross-cutting guarantees live in one place: ink that tracks the deck, the frosted surface that survives a photographic deck, the touch-target floor, the submission lock across an iframe remount, host-delegated image upload, and the deck font on a `<button>` (which does not inherit it). A rebuild re-opens every one of those, silently, and looks fine until the deck turns dark.

criteria.title: Deck font is LOADED into the iframe, not just referenced
criteria.test: **Scope.** Fires whenever the audience surface renders text in the deck font — it binds `xprops.presentation.fontFamily` (directly, or via a `deckFont` computed, or a global `font-family: inherit` that ultimately resolves to it) to its text. A surface that renders only in the bundled default face PASSes vacuously. **Rule.** The host forwards only the deck font's **NAME** (`xprops.presentation.fontFamily`), never the file. The audience surface is a **cross-origin iframe** and does **not** inherit its parent's `@font-face` rules — so naming the font is not enough; the face has to be **loaded into this iframe** or the browser falls back to **serif** (Times) for **all** audience text. Call the shared `useDeckFont(fontFamily)` helper (injects the Google-Fonts `<link>`, idempotent, no-ops for the bundled Plus Jakarta Sans). Binding / inheriting the deck font **without** loading the face is a **FAIL**.

criteria.title: Selection controls and the "your pick" indicator track the deck
criteria.test: **Rule.** The controls that carry choice and selection — a Radio, a Checkbox, and the ring/edge that marks the row a participant picked — must read from the deck, not from a fixed brand colour. Two facets, both reported (AHAM-701): 1. **A checked Radio / Checkbox uses the deck ACCENT, not Ant's fixed `colorPrimary` purple.** The checked fill/dot is `presentationColorPalette[0]` (published as a custom property like `--aha-control-accent`, brand primary only as a fallback). A `<a-radio>` / `<a-checkbox>` left on the theme's purple is the same fixed-colour FAIL as a purple submit button — it reads purple on a green deck. 2. **The SELECTED-answer ring / state edge uses the deck's TEXT colour, not a fixed near-black or a deepened accent.** A ring hard-coded to black / `#1A1A1A` — or an accent deepened toward black for contrast on its own fill — vanishes on a dark deck, where the text is light. The ring must be `xprops.slide.textColour` so it is the very colour the deck author already chose to read against their background. The accent still marks the pick on the CONTROL (the check/dot) and in the label weight; the ring's job is visibility, and deck ink is what keeps it visible on light AND dark decks.

criteria.title: A filled slider / progress track carries a deck-ink edge
criteria.test: **Rule.** A slider's FILLED (accent) portion, and a progress fill, must carry the SAME deck-ink hairline the empty rail already has, so a coloured fill does not sink into a same-hue deck (AHAM-701 issue 4). The edge is the deck ink at the shared audience border alpha (10%, one value for every track and panel hairline; a tappable chip, the dashed image drop area and an answer row's radio / checkbox control use the ink at 20%), reached through `currentColor` so it tracks the deck — the same edge the unfilled rail uses, extended onto the fill.

criteria.title: Body copy and option labels use the audience default body size
criteria.test: **Rule.** Primary body text, answer-option labels, chip labels and tags render at the audience DEFAULT body size, 16px (`--aha-size-l`) (AHAM-701 issue 2). 14px (`--aha-size-default`) is legitimate ONLY on secondary metadata — a vote-count chip, a percentage, a character counter — never on the option label or main body copy. **Token trap:** `--aha-size-sm` is **12px**, not the 14px 'text-sm', so primary copy bound to `--aha-size-sm` FAILs even though the name reads 'small text'.

criteria.title: A horizontal slider's rail lines up with its end labels, never an uneven leftover margin
criteria.test: **Rule.** A horizontal audience slider's rail lines up with its min/max end labels: flush under them, or inset by the same intended amount on both sides (`<aha-scale-slider>` insets 16px). FAIL on an accidental, uneven leftover Ant component margin (e.g. a default `margin: 10px 6px`-ish inset on a rail whose end-label row spans the full width) that shifts the rail so it no longer lines up with the captions it belongs to (AHAM-701 issue 3).

criteria.title: Distinct labelled sections are separated by ≥24px
criteria.test: **Rule.** An audience screen that stacks two or more DISTINCT labelled sections — a section being a heading/label plus the control group it introduces, e.g. `Choose a lot` + the answer options, then `Set your bid` + the slider — puts at least **24px** of vertical space between one section and the next (AHAM-701 issue). The small tappable/field gap (8–16px) is for spacing rows or fields INSIDE one group; when that same small gap is used between whole sections, the heading of the second section crowds the last control of the first and the two steps read as one undifferentiated stack, so a participant loses the "pick a lot, THEN set a bid" structure. The section rhythm is the audience mirror of the settings `fieldGapClass` (24px between config blocks).

criteria.title: A repeated row holds its DECLARED range, in one shape, with no fixed void
criteria.test: **Rule.** A row that repeats — an item plus its control — is designed for the whole range of content it is *allowed* to hold, not for the content it happened to be posed with. Three things follow, and each one is a way the same design fails.

criteria.title: Participant identity shown only when the slide opts into the host join flow
criteria.test: **Rule.** The audience iframe never knows the participant's own name, emoji or team unless the slide type opts into the host's join/identity flow. The host populates `audienceName` / `audienceEmoji` (and team) ONLY when the manifest declares `setting.enableAudienceJoinPresentation: true` — that flag is what makes the host run the QR/join step and hand the identity down. Without it those refs are `undefined` in production, so any identity affordance the plugin draws — an "Adding as `<name>`" row, a "you are …" chip, a name/emoji/avatar badge — renders blank or falls back to a hard-coded stand-in on a real phone. The trap is that the playground broker *fakes* a sample name (e.g. "Sample participant"), so the row looks populated in preview and the defect only appears in the product. The plugin must also never PROMPT for identity itself — the host owns that flow (reuse-host-capabilities: "Never prompt for identity yourself").

criteria.title: A form field sits on a chosen legible surface with deck-tracking ink
criteria.test: **Rule.** An audience `<input>` / `<textarea>` / `<select>` is a *bounded field* the participant has to find and read their own typing in — it needs an explicitly chosen surface and ink, not the defaults it inherits. C5 says the plugin picks its own background *in general*; this criterion makes that testable for FORM FIELDS specifically, because the two ways a field goes wrong are both invisible in the playground: **a. The field has an explicitly chosen surface.** A form field left transparent (no `background` set) borrows whatever is behind it. On the white playground that looks like a field; on a photographic or dark presenter deck the box vanishes and reads as *no field at all* — the participant can't see where to tap or what they typed. Give it the frosted audience surface (the same chosen surface the rest of the plugin uses — e.g. a `color-mix` frost / a near-opaque panel), not `transparent` and not "inherit from the deck".

criteria.title: A Select / dropdown popup opens below, themes its panel, and stays in the iframe box
criteria.test: **Rule.** A native `<select>` or a custom popup menu (an Ant `Select`, a combobox) has a second surface — the open PANEL — that the closed control's styling does not cover. Three things must hold, and each is a separate way the same control fails: **a. Opens BELOW the closed control, not over it.** The panel drops beneath the field so the closed control stays visible and the participant keeps their place. A panel that renders *on top of* the closed control (default `placement` flipped, or an absolutely-positioned menu with a negative offset) hides the very field the participant just tapped and reads as the control disappearing.

criteria.title: Exactly one instruction line per audience screen — a second, restating line FAILs
criteria.test: **Rule.** An audience screen carries at most ONE instruction line telling the participant what to do. A second line — a separate instruction elsewhere on the screen, or an inner prompt / placeholder / hint beside the control — that RESTATES the same task is redundant: it says nothing the first line didn't, and on the shrink-wrapped mobile surface two instructions compete for the eye and push the actual control down the fold. De-duplicate to a single instruction.

criteria.title: A full SubmittedCard is only for a swipe-card interaction; every other slide locks its answer in place
criteria.test: **Rule.** The separate, full-surface `SubmittedCard` component — the one that REPLACES the whole answer surface with a standalone "you're in" card — is only appropriate for a **swipe-card interaction**: a slide where the participant's answer IS a card they swipe or tap (true-or-false's swipe/tap-a-card, this-or-that, and the like). There the card is the mechanic, so swapping to a submitted card is continuous with what the participant just did.

criteria.title: An audience text field's LABEL tracks the deck ink at the 16px body size
criteria.test: **Rule.** The label ABOVE an audience `<input>` / `<textarea>` ("Your answer", "Your name", …) is read against the DECK, not against the field's own chosen surface — so it obeys the same two rules the deck body copy does, and the two defaults it inherits from Ant's `Form.Item` label both break it: **a. The label tracks the deck ink.** The label colour is `xprops.slide.textColour`, NOT a fixed dark ink (`#000` / `#111` / `rgba(0,0,0,.85)` / Ant's `colorTextHeading`). A fixed dark label is white-on-white — invisible — the moment the deck is dark; a fixed light one dies on a light deck. This is the surface-ink invariant (C24) applied to the label, which sits on the deck rather than on the field's frosted fill.

criteria.title: A field's character counter sits INSIDE it, reveals on focus, counts DOWN, in muted field ink
criteria.test: **Rule.** A character counter on an audience `<input>` / `<textarea>` mirrors the shipped settings `CountedTextarea` / `CountedInput` pattern — four things, and each has a specific wrong default that this criterion catches: **a. Inside the field, not below it.** The counter is positioned INSIDE the field box — bottom-right for a `<textarea>`, right-aligned for a single-line `<input>` — not on a separate line beneath the field. A counter below the field adds a row of chrome and detaches the count from the thing it counts.

criteria.title: An ACTIVE audience submit button is passed the deck accent, not left on the component's purple fallback
criteria.test: **Rule.** This repo's submit CTA is the shared library component (`SubmitButton` / `AudienceSubmitButton` from `@/iframe/audience`), whose fill DEFAULTS to the fixed brand purple and only tracks the deck when it is passed `:accent="presentationColorPalette[0]"`. So an ACTIVE (answerable) submit button MUST bind that accent. On the build-less Developer Platform the submit is `<aha-audience-submit>` from `lib/audience.js`, which reads the deck accent from `--aha-color-primary` once `applyDeck` has run: it PASSes with no accent prop, and FAILs when `applyDeck` is never called.

criteria.title: One accent per deck — the same --aha-color-primary as the canvas
criteria.test: The selected chip, checked control and submit fill use `presentationColorPalette[0]` published as `--aha-color-primary` on `:root` — the same value the presenter canvas uses. FAIL when the audience recomputes the accent (a 'towardInk' selection colour beside a raw submit colour), when two controls on one screen show different 'primary' colours, or when a semantic colour (success teal, error red) is used as a data or column colour. Picking only the label ink by contrast is correct.

criteria.title: Borders are hairlines and radius follows the DS scale
criteria.test: A bounded white card has a 1px `--aha-border-default` (#E3E3E3) border and 12px radius; a deck field, track or panel a 1px 10% ink border (a tappable chip, the dashed drop area and an answer row's radio / checkbox control take the ink at 20%); the dashed image drop area is the one 2px edge, dashed; option tiles, inputs and the submit button 8px. FAIL on any other 2px (or heavier) outline, on outlines at heavy ink (e.g. 55% textColour) on chips, cards or inputs, or on a rectangular container above 12px radius.

criteria.title: One fixed dark ink: #1A1A1A
criteria.test: Any fixed dark ink — a label on a light accent, a fallback ink — is `--aha-text-default` #1A1A1A. FAIL on the retired indigo `#1A1A2E` as text ink, or `#000` as the dark label on the accent.

criteria.title: Interactive states animate with motion tokens on persistent nodes
criteria.test: Hover, selected, pressed and expanded states transition with `--aha-motion-*` durations and `--aha-ease-*` curves on nodes that persist. FAIL when states snap with no transition, use a bare duration literal, or when the screen is rebuilt with `innerHTML =` on each change so the transition never fires.

criteria.title: Stage steppers and comboboxes are the DS elements, current stage in ink
criteria.test: *(Fires when the audience screen shows a stage indicator or a type-to-pick field. N/A otherwise.)* On the Developer Platform a stage indicator is `<aha-stepper>` and a type-to-pick field (owner, name) is `<aha-autocomplete size="large">`, both from `lib/all.js`. FAIL on a hand-rolled stepper or a hand-built `<input>` + suggestion list / custom `<div role="listbox">`, and FAIL when the current stage is painted with the primary accent instead of ink.

targets.use: the <aha-chart> chart types, the palette attribute (brand | deck) and the chart types it does not ship

criteria.title: A result/data chart is <aha-chart>, not a hand-rolled or third-party chart
criteria.test: Every result or data chart on an app screen, Report, canvas or audience view is rendered with the DS `<aha-chart>` element for a chart type its live contract ships. A hand-rolled SVG/canvas/CSS-bar chart, or a third-party chart library (Chart.js, Recharts, ECharts, D3-drawn, Highcharts, ApexCharts, Victory, Nivo), fails. The one exception is `@ant-design/plots` for a chart type `<aha-chart>` does not ship.

criteria.title: <aha-chart> uses the palette for its surface
criteria.test: App screens such as Report use `palette="brand"` (the default); the presenting or audience canvas uses `palette="deck"` with the deck's `colors` and `ink`. A canvas chart left on the brand palette, or an app-screen chart painted with hand-picked series colours, fails.

report-images.surface: reports (static report images and read-only report pages)

targets.use: the report rules for images and report pages: size, type, series order, end labels, twin axes, gaps, zero runs, ticks and formats, titles, missing glyphs, report tables, number plates and glyphs
the chart a report page uses and a static chart copies: line and column geometry (end labels, twin axis, gaps, negatives, reference line, x labels thinned on a phone)
the number plate: <aha-stat-tile look="accent"> on a report page, drawn to the same spec in an image (C12)

rule 3.11 (light grey zebra rows and pale pink plates in reports, image and page alike), 3.6 (light grey for table surfaces), the chart colours (8.1 to 8.4), text on Vivid Pink at 5% (6.5) and rises and falls (7.3)

criteria.title: Size and density: an image is a 2x export under 1 MB; a page reflows from 360 px
criteria.test: **Rule.** A report image is drawn at 2x (a full-width chart is 1,200 × 675 px at 1x, exported at 2,400 × 1,350), with text no smaller than 12 px at 1x for ticks and notes and 14 px for labels, values and table text, a 24 px white margin, one chart, table or plate row per image, and a file under 1 MB. A 1x export that blurs in Slack, 9 px tick labels, three charts crammed into one PNG, or a 3 MB file fails. A report page is white, uses the same text sizes, may hold many charts, tables and plate rows, and reflows from a 360 px phone with no horizontal page scroll (only a wide table may scroll sideways); a page that overflows at 390 px, or x labels cut to one character, fails.

criteria.title: Type: Plus Jakarta Sans, 400 and 600 only
criteria.test: **Rule.** All text is Plus Jakarta Sans from the DS font files, in weight 400 (ticks, captions, notes, table text) or 600 (titles, values, end labels, table headers). DejaVu Sans, Arial or a renderer default, a bold 700, a light 300 or a second typeface fails.

criteria.title: Series follow the chart order; past four parts, the top 3 plus Other
criteria.test: **Rule.** Series are coloured in the chart order (Vivid Pink, black, Vivid Pink at 30%, light grey #A8A8A8), the main series first. A breakdown with more than four parts shows the top three by value and folds the rest into Other, in light grey and last. A fifth colour, a palette in another order, Other placed first or in pink, or two Other slots (a source Other beside the folded one) fails.

criteria.title: Every line carries a non-overlapping end-value label
criteria.test: **Rule.** Each line shows its latest value at its right end, formatted like its axis. Labels never overlap one another or a line end: when two would touch they are pushed apart and joined to their lines by a short leader in the series colour. A line with no end label, two labels printed on top of each other, or a moved label with no leader fails. A line in Vivid Pink at 30% or grey without its value written fails (colour rule 8.3).

criteria.title: A twin axis is named in the legend
criteria.test: **Rule.** A right axis is used only for a series in a different unit, shares the left axis's grid lines, and the legend names each series' axis (Sessions (left axis), Conversion (right axis)). A twin-axis chart whose legend does not say which series reads on which axis, or a right axis for a series in the same unit, fails.

criteria.title: A missing period breaks the line
criteria.test: **Rule.** A period with no data breaks the line: it is never plotted as zero and never bridged by a segment, and a point with no neighbour keeps its marker. A line that drops to zero for missing data, or draws straight across a gap, fails.

criteria.title: A real run of zeros carries a note
criteria.test: **Rule.** When a series is really zero for three or more periods in a row (not missing), a short note in secondary text on the chart says so, such as No sessions from 3 to 9 Oct. A flat zero run with no note, which a reader cannot tell from missing data, fails.

criteria.title: Tick density and number formats
criteria.test: **Rule.** The y axis has 3 to 6 divisions on round steps and starts at zero for counts; x labels never overlap and the latest period is always labelled; values of 1,000 and above are written with K or M and at most one decimal (12K, 1.3M); percentages are whole (46%); the axis, the end labels and any table use the same format. Overlapping or rotated x labels, 9 y ticks, 12,345.67 on an axis, 46.23% or a format that differs between axis and labels fails.

criteria.title: Sentence-case titles with no em or en dashes
criteria.test: **Rule.** Titles and labels are sentence case and say what and when (Weekly sign-ups, last 12 weeks). No em dash or en dash appears anywhere on the image; a range uses to (3 to 9 Oct) and a pause uses a comma. Title Case, ALL CAPS, an em or en dash, or a title ending in a full stop fails.

criteria.title: No missing glyphs; marks are DS files, not font characters
criteria.test: **Rule.** Every character renders: the renderer has a fallback font for the scripts the data can hold, so a Vietnamese or accented name never shows as empty boxes. Arrows and status marks are DS glyphs (<aha-icon> on a report page, lib/static-icons in an image), not typed as ▲ ▼ ✓ characters or emoji. A tofu box, a missing accent or a font-character arrow fails.

criteria.title: Report tables: zebra rows, no dividers, pink header rule
criteria.test: **Rule.** A table in a report, image or page, has zebra rows alternating white and light grey (#F7F7F7, --aha-bg-container-secondary) and no horizontal row dividers, header labels in black semibold over a 2px Vivid Pink rule, figures in black tabular numerals aligned right and text aligned left. Plain white rows with no striping, pale pink (Vivid Pink at 5%) rows, grey or pink-filled headers, pink text, horizontal row dividers, vertical rules or coloured status cells fail. Tables on screens of the product app, its Report screens included, are judged on the table surface instead and keep plain rows. (Colour rules 3.11 and 3.6.)

criteria.title: Number plates: Vivid Pink at 5% card, black text, direction by shape
criteria.test: **Rule.** A number plate (the KPI tile) is a flat Vivid Pink at 5% card with a 4px Vivid Pink top bar and 8px corners, black label (400) and value (600), the change as an absolute number and a whole percent, and the comparison caption in secondary text: <aha-stat-tile look="accent"> on a report page, any number of them, and the same spec drawn in an image. A rise is black with the up arrow; a fall is white on a black pill with the down arrow. A grey or white-only plate with no brand colour, pink text on the card, a green or red change, a change with no arrow, or a drop shadow fails. (Colour rule 3.11.)

criteria.title: Status glyphs come from the DS: <aha-icon> on a page, lib/static-icons in an image
criteria.test: **Rule.** Every status mark in a report (rise, fall, no change, warning, pending, progress) is a DS glyph called by its registry name, at 12, 16, 24 or 32 px, in ink or white: <aha-icon> on a report page, a file from lib/static-icons in an image. A drawn triangle or circle, an emoji, an icon from another set or a recoloured glyph fails.

targets.use: the DS tokens and components a screen must reuse (U4); the Nielsen Norman Group heuristics are at https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/

criteria.title: Visibility of system status
criteria.test: Every action and wait shows the system's state in the UI: loading, saving, progress, success, error, and the current location or selection. Evidence: a loading/pending state for each async call, and visible feedback after each action. N/A when the change has no async work, action or navigation (a colour, spacing or label edit).

criteria.title: Match between the system and the real world
criteria.test: Words, icons and order use the user's language and real-world conventions, not internal or technical terms (no ids, enum names or API vocabulary on screen); information appears in a natural, logical order. N/A when the change adds no visible text, icon or ordering.

criteria.title: User control and freedom
criteria.test: A user who acts by mistake can leave: cancel, close, undo or back on every dialog, form, multi-step flow and destructive action, with a clear exit that does not lose their work unasked. N/A when the change adds no dialog, flow or reversible action.

criteria.title: Consistency and standards
criteria.test: The same thing looks and behaves the same way: DS components, tokens and platform conventions, with one term per concept across the screen and its neighbours. A bespoke control where the DS ships one fails. N/A when the change touches no visible element.

criteria.title: Error prevention
criteria.test: The design stops the error before it happens: constraints, sensible defaults, inline validation, a confirmation or undo for destructive or irreversible actions, and no submit that can be sent in a known-invalid state. N/A when the change has no input, destructive action or irreversible step.

criteria.title: Recognition rather than recall
criteria.test: Options, actions and context are visible or one step away; the user is never asked to remember a value from another screen or step. Labels persist (no placeholder-only fields), and the current state is shown. N/A when the change adds no input, choice or multi-step context.

criteria.title: Flexibility and efficiency of use
criteria.test: Frequent tasks are quick for experts and clear for novices: sensible defaults, keyboard access and shortcuts, bulk or repeat actions where the task repeats. N/A when the change adds no task a user repeats.

criteria.title: Aesthetic and minimalist design
criteria.test: Each screen carries only what the task needs: one clear primary action, no competing or decorative content, and hierarchy that puts the important thing first. Extra information fails unless it earns its place. N/A when the change adds no content or controls.

criteria.title: Help users recognise, diagnose, and recover from errors
criteria.test: An error is in plain language, says what went wrong and offers a way back (retry, fix the field, contact), placed at the point of the problem and not by colour alone. N/A when the change has no error path; an error state that is missing where one can occur is a FAIL.

criteria.title: Help and documentation
criteria.test: Anything not self-evident has help at the point of use: a hint, tooltip, empty-state guidance or a link to docs, short and task-focused. N/A when the screen is self-evident or the change adds no unfamiliar concept.

the DS Marketing section library every band of a page comes from, with the padding, widths and breakpoints each section ships
the web background rules W5 cites by id (3.2 to 3.5, 3.8, 3.10) and the button rules W4 cites (6.1, 6.2)
the icon names <aha-icon> may draw (W6)

criteria.title: Every band is a DS Marketing section
criteria.test: Each full-width band of the page (site header, hero, features, numbers, logos, testimonials, pricing, comparison table, FAQ, closing banner, footer) is a DS Marketing section (Navigation, Hero, Features, Numbers, Logos, Testimonials, Pricing, Comparison table, FAQ, Footer banner, Footer, with Cards inside a section): its root class and markup are the section's snippet, with only copy, images and the layout choice changed. A band built by hand (its own classes, its own grid, a restyled copy of a section) fails, whatever it looks like; the fix is the matching section, or a DSN ticket for a missing one. On a page the Logos strip always comes straight after the hero (the Hero section, after the Navigation): after a Vivid Pink hero it is the hero's last child, with aha-logos--brand, so the Splash runs behind it; after a White hero it is the band directly below; never later in the page and never left out of that slot and placed mid-page; the strip that follows it follows W5. A page with no customer logos has no Logos strip. A Logos strip after Features, Numbers, Testimonials or any other section, or a page that places it anywhere but directly below the hero, fails. N/A when the change is a single section on its own, not a page. Every DS class the markup uses is styled by the page's CSS: paste the whole section snippet, its CSS included, never the markup with part of the CSS (screen-lint `ds-class-without-css` catches the pasted-in-part case; a page with no CSS of its own for a section is checked by render).

criteria.title: Sections keep their shipped spacing levels and gutter
criteria.test: Every section keeps the spacing it ships and never overrides it. Section spacing uses only the four levels: Section (--aha-section-space-block, 96 px; 64 at 767 px; 48 at 479 px) for a section's top and bottom padding, Header (--aha-section-space-header, 64/48/32) below a heading block and between a copy column and its content column, Group (--aha-section-space-group, 48/32/24) between groups inside a section and before a closing call to action, Item (--aha-section-space-item, 32/24/16) between repeated items. The visible space between two neighbouring sections' content is one Section level: across a surface change each side keeps its Section padding up to the edge, and on a shared surface the second section drops its top padding (tokens.css applies this to direct siblings), so 192 px of white between two White sections fails; the Logos strip sits one Group below the content of the section above it, on that section's surface: after a Vivid Pink hero it is nested inside the hero as its last child (aha-logos--brand), so the hero's Splash runs behind it with no seam and no flat pink strip; a Vivid Pink Logos strip placed after the hero as its own band fails (screen-lint `band-after-brand-hero`). Side padding is one gutter, --aha-web-gutter: --aha-space-64 on desktop, --aha-space-24 at 767 px and below, --aha-space-16 at 479 px and below; Heroes, page Headers, Footer and Navigation keep 32 px sides above 767 px. A button sits --aha-space-32 below its own block's text (24 at 479 px). Sections sit flush. An overridden section padding, level or gutter, a raw px value in place of a level, a level switched by the page's own breakpoint, a raw button margin added on top, or a margin, spacer element or divider added between sections fails. N/A when the page has a single section. The visible gap between two bands is exactly one Section step (96 px at 1440, 64 at 768, 48 at 375, `--aha-section-space-block`): the page adds no margin, padding, gap, spacer or divider of its own between bands, and never wraps two same-surface bands in their own elements, which doubles the padding (screen-lint `section-gap` fails these static cases; the measured gap at 1440, 768 and 375 is checked by render only).

criteria.title: Content width is capped and measured
criteria.test: Section content is capped at 1280 px and centred; a section heading block stays within 720 px and its lead text within 44ch, as the sections ship. Content stretched to the full viewport width, a lead paragraph wider than 44ch, or a container cap raised or removed fails. N/A when the page has no section with a heading or lead text. screen-lint reports it as content-width-uncapped.

criteria.title: One H1, one primary action per section, labelled for the page, the hero's action repeated
criteria.test: The page has exactly one <h1>, in the Hero section. No section has more than one primary button (colour rule 6.1; on Vivid Pink the button is the secondary Button, rule 6.2); no more than two buttons sit side by side, a primary and a secondary. The Sign up or primary call to action label is written for the page's context, a verb plus what the visitor gets (Use this template on a template page, Create your quiz free on a quiz-maker page, Start free on pricing); Get started free is only the fallback when no context-specific label fits. When the page has a closing Footer banner it repeats the hero's primary call to action with the same label. Two H1s, an H1 outside the hero, two primary buttons in one section, three or more buttons in a row, or a closing banner with a different main action or label, or the generic Get started free on a page whose context has a more specific label, fails. N/A for the closing-action part when the page has no closing banner. screen-lint reports it as missing-h1, multiple-h1 or multiple-primary-buttons.

criteria.title: Band backgrounds follow the colour rules
criteria.test: Band backgrounds follow brand/colour-rules.json 3.2 to 3.5, 3.8 and 3.10: white by default; coloured bands are Vivid Pink or pale pink (a Features section with the aha-features--accent class, never an inline background: var(--aha-bg-accent) style); a landing page (a page of full-width sections opened by a Hero layout) has a Vivid Pink hero #E70E68 (rule 3.5), its Hero in the Vivid Pink state (`--brand` class), with the body then alternating white and pale pink starting with white; a full white section always sits between two coloured bands; the section directly after the hero and its Logos strip is always full white, never pale pink or another tint; at most two Vivid Pink bands, a Vivid Pink hero being one; no black band; no gradient. A pale pink or other tinted band directly after the Logos strip, any coloured band (Vivid Pink Logos strip included) placed straight after a Vivid Pink hero as its own section (screen-lint `band-after-brand-hero`), two coloured bands touching, a third Vivid Pink band, a Darker Pink hero background (Darker Pink is only the Splash hooks on Vivid Pink, rule 5.1), an inline --aha-bg-accent background on a section, a full-width light grey band, or a Hero left in the White state on a landing page (the snippet default is White: switch it to Vivid Pink) fails: light grey belongs to cards inside a section. N/A when every band is white.

criteria.title: Imagery is real and icons come from the registry
criteria.test: Every picture is an with meaningful alt text (or alt="" when decorative) showing a product screenshot, a committed photo, or the DS placeholder marketing-assets/image-placeholder.svg. A photo of people, customers or an event comes only from the AhaSlides Drive photo library or Customer Love; a stock photo (Unsplash, Pexels, Picsum, Shutterstock, iStock, Getty, Adobe Stock, Freepik and the like) fails. Stock clip art, emoji used as icons, gradient blobs, glassmorphism (backdrop-filter blur panels), decorative 3D shapes, a CSS-drawn picture standing in for an image, a screenshot cropped by object-fit: cover, a screenshot padded, letterboxed or placed on a plain canvas inside its file, or carrying its own background margin, a stretched or distorted image, and any icon not drawn by from the registry fail. One narrow exception, for photos only in the multi-image heroes and Gallery layouts and the Features Sticky stack: a tilted photo in the photo stack or floating images, sitting in the photo frame (an 8 px white border and a 1 px ring, no shadow), and cover-cropped photo cells of mixed size in a bento, collage or masonry layout pass. A tilted or cover-cropped screenshot, a tilted photo outside those layouts, or a tilted photo with a drop shadow instead of the frame fails. A light grey (#F6F6F6 or #F7F7F7) border-left or background on a blockquote, a rail or an image frame, fails. N/A when the page has no pictures and no icons. screen-lint reports it as img-no-alt, img-empty-alt or stock-photo (a stock-photo host in an image address).

criteria.title: The site header is the Navigation section with the product lockup
criteria.test: The page's site header is the DS Navigation section, so its brand is <aha-product-lockup> (the app-shell surface's C1 holds the brand rule itself). A hand-built header, a logo file next to a text span, or a letter tile in its place fails. N/A when the page is embedded with no site header of its own (an in-product help or upgrade page under the app's own header). screen-lint reports it as brand-not-lockup or missing-navigation.

criteria.title: Responsive at 1440, 768 and 375
criteria.test: The page is checked at 1440, 768 and 375 px wide with no horizontal scroll at any of them; multi-column sections stack to one column; a stacked image sits below its text (text first) in every section; calls to action keep the xl button height the sections ship and nothing tappable is under 24 by 24 px. One exception passes: a Comparison table with four or five compared columns that keeps its columns at 375 px and scrolls sideways inside its own table frame, with the feature column sticky, while the page itself does not scroll. A fixed width or min-width that overflows a phone, a section that stays multi-column at 375 px (other than that table), images flipping above and below text from section to section, or a shrunken call to action fails. N/A only when the judge has nothing that sets layout (copy-only change). screen-lint --surface=website --measure renders the page at 1440, 768 and 375 px and reports horizontal scroll.

criteria.title: Motion is the DS script, staggered, and optional
criteria.test: Motion is the shipped DS script (lib/marketing-motion.js) plus hover transitions: elements reveal on scroll with a fade and short slide staggered 60 to 100 ms apart, a real photo in a `*__frame` wrapper drifts inside that frame with a light parallax (the frame never moves, the picture drifts at most 6% of the frame height and never more than 48 px, and a screenshot has no frame wrapper so does not drift) and enters with a fade and a settle from about 1.08x scale as it scrolls into view, and Numbers values count up from 0 to the written value once in view, all timed with --aha-motion-* and --aha-ease-* tokens and shown at their final state under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. The shipped marquee loops pass: the Logos strip, and the photo marquees (the Hero image marquee and Gallery marquee rows) with their pause while hovered or focused and their stop under reduced motion, and no Pause button (as on the Logos strip); at most one looping photo band per page, never next to the Logos strip. The hero may carry exactly one video that plays by itself: a `<video>` with autoplay, muted, loop, playsinline and a poster, paused under prefers-reduced-motion (lib/marketing-motion.js pauses it); a hero video with controls and no autoplay passes too. A photo loop without the pause or the reduced-motion stop, or a second looping photo band, is looping decorative animation and fails. Scroll-jacking, a hand-written scroll or parallax script, parallax beyond a light drift of the picture inside its frame (a hero, text, a photo frame or a whole section moving), an autoplaying carousel, a second autoplaying video or one outside the hero, an autoplaying hero video missing muted, loop, playsinline or the poster, or one that keeps playing under prefers-reduced-motion, looping decorative animation, a bare duration literal, numbers that show their final value with no count-up, or motion with no reduced-motion fallback fails. N/A only when the page has no Marketing section. screen-lint reports it as motion-library, motion-own-script or motion-own-animation. The page's marketing-motion.js is the current DS file, never an edited or older copy: screen-lint `motion-script-copy` compares it with lib/marketing-motion.js at lint time (no stored hash), so a DS release is picked up with no list to update.

criteria.title: Image-led sections show every image large and whole
criteria.test: A section where readers compare the pictures (themes, slide types) is image-led: it uses the Cards aha-marketing-cards__grid--image-led layout, with at most 2 columns on desktop so every image is at least half the content width, 4 items as 2 by 2, an odd count with the first item as a wide feature card (image two thirds, title beside it), and 1 column below 768 px, and no image is cropped. A text-led section (steps, benefits, use cases) follows W11 for its column count. Pictures to compare in 3 or 4 columns, an image under half the content width, or a cropped image in an image-led section fails. Templates are the exception: a grid of Template cards (template thumbnails) is always 3 columns at 992 px and wider (the Cards aha-marketing-cards__grid--templates grid), n full rows of 3, so the template count is a multiple of 3; never the 2-column image-led layout, never 4 as 2 by 2, never an empty slot or a centred lone card; the 768 to 991 px and phone layouts stay as Cards ships them. Templates in 2 columns, 4 or 5 templates, or an image-led or count-balanced template grid at desktop fails. N/A when no section compares pictures. A text-led section with four or more points is the Cards grid, and each card description is 25 words or fewer (screen-lint `card-description-long` counts the words of a Cards, Features or Numbers description; judging that a section is text-led with four or more points, and whether a cut description still says enough, is for the judge and the render).

criteria.title: Card and feature grids are balanced
criteria.test: A card or feature grid (not a templates grid, which W10 fixes at 3 by n) has no empty column slot and is not off-centre: the column count follows the item count (1 item one centred column, 2 items 2 columns, 3 items 3, 4 items 2 by 2, 5 or more 3 columns with the short last row centred). The shipped Cards grid, Features icon grid and Numbers stats do this by default; 2 stats in a 3-column row, or a page-only override to fix it, fails. Two cards in a 3-column grid with an empty third slot, 4 items as 3 plus 1, a last row pinned to the left, or a `grid-template-columns` override that leaves a gap fails. N/A when the page has no card, feature or stats grid.

criteria.title: No layout fatigue
criteria.test: No section shows more than 3 alternating image/text rows, no two alternating-row sections sit back to back, numbered steps use the DS Steps row (Cards aha-marketing-cards__grid--row; four or more steps are a Cards grid of Step cards, or the Features swipeable card scroller with images) and not alternating rows or Features Tabs, a Tabs section holds parallel choices with each description at most 90 characters, and a section moved to another layout keeps every point, step and image (five steps are five Step cards with their images), and no two consecutive sections share the same layout. 4 or more alternating rows in one section, two alternating sections in a row (for example 6 zig-zag rows in a run), numbered steps or a how it works built as alternating rows or as Tabs, a tab description over 90 characters, steps cut to fewer cards or their images dropped when a section changes layout, or two neighbouring sections with the same layout fails. N/A when the page has fewer than two sections with a body layout. Numbered steps are the Cards Steps row (`aha-marketing-cards__grid--row`) with the DS number ring (`aha-marketing-card__number`), never a hand-built layout or numbers drawn by hand (screen-lint `step-numbers`).

criteria.title: Testimonials and FAQ are the current DS sections
criteria.test: Every testimonials band is one of the current DS Testimonials layouts (Simple left aligned, Case study cards, Quote cards) and every FAQ band is the current FAQ section (marketing/faq.json), with the markup and CSS pasted unchanged and only copy and images edited. A hand-built or older copy fails: an `aha-testimonials--centered-01` or other retired modifier, a testimonial without the layout's classes, an FAQ without `aha-faq__trigger` buttons carrying `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` and the plus/minus icon, or a hand-made accordion. N/A when the page has no testimonials or FAQ.

criteria.title: One type ramp across the page
criteria.test: Each text role uses one DS type token on the whole page, so the same role has the same size, weight and family in every section: section heading (h2) `--aha-size-h2` semibold; section lead and quote text the lead clamp (16 to 20 px) regular; alternating row title `--aha-size-h4` semibold; every item or card title (Cards, Features, Steps, image-led cards, Numbers stat title, Pricing benefit, FAQ question) `--aha-size-xl` semibold; body `--aha-size-l` regular; meta or caption `--aha-size-default` regular; badge label (the New badge on a Template card) `--aha-size-sm` semibold; stat number the stat clamp (40 to 48 px) semibold; all in Plus Jakarta Sans; no eyebrow (a small uppercase label above a heading) on any section heading, the hero and page header included. An eyebrow above a section heading, card titles regular in one section and semibold in another, quote text at a heading size or semibold, h2 sizes that differ between sections, or any heading in Nunito (`--aha-font-display`) or a page or Webflow font fails. N/A when the page has a single section. Body text and every h1 to h6 resolve to Plus Jakarta Sans (`--aha-font-product`), never a page, Webflow or fallback-first font (screen-lint `page-font` reads the page's own rules for html, body and headings; a font set by a linked stylesheet is checked by render).

criteria.title: Content card links and section link-out buttons open in a new tab, Sign up does not
criteria.test: Every content card link and see-more link to another page in a Marketing section (Template, Testimonial or case-study, Integration, Article, Feature and Use-case card links) opens in a new tab: `target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener"`, plus a visually-hidden "(opens in a new tab)" inside the link for screen readers (`aha-marketing-card__visually-hidden`, `aha-testimonials__visually-hidden` or `aha-features__visually-hidden`), so readers keep the page open and stay longer. So do the section link-out buttons that go to another page (Browse all templates, See all integrations, Read customer stories, Read the docs): the same `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener"` and hidden new-tab text (`aha-testimonials__visually-hidden`, `aha-faq__visually-hidden`). In the Footer every link that leaves AhaSlides (the G2 and Training Magazine Network award badges, the DMCA badge, the System status page and the social channels) opens in a new tab with `rel="noopener"` and a new-tab cue in its label, all alike. Sign up and the hero's primary call to action (Hero, Features, Numbers, Pricing, Footer banner), the Navigation links and the Footer links to AhaSlides pages stay in the same tab. A content card link that opens in the same tab, a new-tab link with no `rel="noopener"` or no hidden new-tab text, a link-out button or an off-site Footer link that opens in the same tab, one off-site Footer badge or social link without the new tab while its neighbours have it, or a Sign up button that opens a new tab fails. N/A when the page has no content card link. screen-lint reports it as card-link-same-tab or new-tab-on-sign-up.

criteria.title: Every button is the DS Button, never restyled
criteria.test: Every button on the page, the Navigation Log in and Sign up, the Join button and every header, section and footer banner call to action included, is <aha-button variant size> (href for a link, type="submit" in a form), and the page's own CSS sets only layout on it (margin, flex, width, order, align-self). A button the page draws itself (a class named button, btn or cta, or a <button>, [role=button] or link given its own fill, border, radius, height or hover) fails, and so does any colour, fill, border, shadow, height or :hover, :active or :focus rule on aha-button, its ::part or a --aha-button-* token, as screen-lint hand-rolled-button reports. N/A when the page has no button.

criteria.title: Section headings follow one alignment rule
criteria.test: A section heading block (h2 and lead, with no eyebrow above the h2) is centred when it sits full width above the content (Features, Numbers, Pricing, Testimonials quote cards, Cards and FAQ in their symmetric layouts, the FAQ title included) and left aligned only when it shares a row or column with the content (a side-header, split-image or featured layout, or the case-study carousel with arrows on the same row). A left aligned heading over a centred or symmetric grid, a centred heading over a left pinned body, a FAQ title pulled left by a page or reset rule, or sections with the same layout shape aligned differently on one page fails. N/A when the page has no section heading.

criteria.title: Every content section ends with one call to action, aligned with its heading
criteria.test: Every Marketing content section after the hero ends with exactly one call to action: the button row the section ships. The Logos strip, Testimonials `simple-left-aligned` (one quote beside its photo, ending on the quote with no button), Pricing (plan buttons), the Footer banner (it is the call to action), Navigation and Footer are exempt. The button row follows its heading: centred under the content when the heading is centred, left under the content or inside the left header when the heading is left aligned. In a split layout (a text column beside a media column: Features `icon-list-photo`, `tabs-screenshots` and an `alternating-screenshots` section with a single row) the button row sits in the text column under the text, left aligned with it (`aha-features__cta--start` inside `aha-features__column`, or the row's own `aha-features__actions` for the single alternating row, with no second row of buttons under the section), even when the eyebrow and heading above are centred; it is never centred under the whole row. Templates, Integrations, case-study (testimonials included) and FAQ sections end with a secondary link to their own page, labelled for it (Browse all templates, See all integrations, Read customer stories, Read the docs); every other content section ends with the hero's primary call to action as a primary button, with the hero's own label and link (the page-specific label W4 asks for, such as Create your quiz free; Sign up is only the example). A content section with no call to action, a lone left button under a centred or symmetric grid, a centred button under a left aligned section, a button centred under a whole split row instead of in its text column, a page-built button next to the shipped one, a Sign up or hero primary call to action that opens a new tab, the hero's primary call to action on a Templates, Integrations, case-study or FAQ section, a section primary whose label differs from the hero's, a link to another page (View more, Learn more) on any other content section, or a bare View more, Learn more or Click here on the four linking sections fails; those four link-out buttons open in a new tab (W15). N/A when the page has no content section.

criteria.title: Testimonials: at most three cards, quotes of similar length, authors on one baseline
criteria.test: In Testimonials the quote and the author block (avatar, name, role) are left aligned together, even in a centred section: avatar, name and role form one row with the name and role stacked and left aligned, and in a row of quote cards the author rows sit on one baseline across cards, names at the same height even when one role wraps to two lines (the shipped grid subgrid, author row aligned to the top of its track). Every card in the row has the same slots in the same order (stars, title, quote, author), and the author row is pinned to the card bottom in the grid and in the carousel track alike. A centred name or role under a left aligned quote, an avatar on its own line, author rows at different heights across cards, or a card with no rating or title beside cards that have them fails. A Testimonials section shows at most 3 testimonial or case cards, and quotes in a row are of similar length: the longest quote within about 1.5 times the characters of the shortest and none over 160 characters, so no card is a wall of text beside two short ones. 4 or more cards, or one long quote beside short ones (for example 240 characters beside 80), fails. N/A when the page has no Testimonials section.
